entries.name: balloon-zinnia
entries.title: Balloon Zinnia
entries.description: Twenty-two egg-shaped petals hinge around a small throat and sit on a short S-curved stem. A 512-wide ramp stripes both of them, and one 14 second clock keeps the sway, the breath, the colour flow and the band pulse in step. The pointer turns the head and swells the petals under it. A tap bobs the flower and squashes it. Raw WebGL2, no extra libraries.

notes.label: The petals are ellipsoids, not a mesh
notes.description: Each petal is an egg hinged at the throat, instanced from a float texture. The stem is a tube from a second texture. One perspective function projects both, and both fragment shaders sample the same 512-wide ramp.

notes.label: One 14 second clock runs four motions
notes.description: The period holds one sway, eight breaths, eight colour flows and six band pulses. They share the clock, so the stripes and the breath stay locked. Grain is off in the base preset. The only noise left is a 1/255 dither so the long blends do not band.

notes.label: No props paints the base preset
notes.description: 22 petals, puff 134, 5 bands, scale 100, grain 0, lean 48, cup 25, phase 60. A second set of numbers (15 petals, lean 50, cup 50, phase 72) only fills a control that is not a finite number.

notes.label: The loop stops when nobody is looking
notes.description: Reduced motion freezes the clock and skips the entrance. A hidden tab or an offscreen host stops the frame loop. If WebGL2 is missing, the canvas hides and the background colour stays.

notes.label: A slow frame drops mesh density
notes.description: Petal longitude and latitude, and the stem's ring count, step down a ladder when a frame runs long. A fast machine stays on the finest mesh, so the ladder does not change the picture there.

entries.check: The bloom recolours and sways as the pointer passes; every palette shows.

entries.name: cell-portrait
entries.title: Cell Portrait
entries.description: A portrait drawn as a grid of circles that join into capsules and thin bridges. The cells shrink from 36px to 7px while the joins reshuffle every 133ms, then the image colors in and the loop runs back out. Dark areas hold the most circles, so a face reads before any color arrives. Canvas 2D and GSAP, timed frame by frame against the reference recording.

notes.label: Source mechanism
notes.description: Measured frame by frame from the reference recording: circles of radius cell/3, thin bridges cell/6 wide, 42% of neighbors joined, cells shrinking from 36px to 7px on a log scale with sine.inOut, and a new layout every 133ms. Darker cells are likelier to draw a circle, and cells above 70% luma never do.

notes.label: Images
notes.description: A transparent PNG keeps its own alpha. On an opaque image the most common border color is keyed out, along with enclosed pockets larger than 0.4% of the image. Smaller regions such as eye whites stay.

notes.label: Edges
notes.description: Only whole cells are drawn, so no circle is cut by the frame and the silhouette outline always closes inside it.

notes.label: Motion and cost
notes.description: Reduced motion holds the full-color frame with no reshuffle. The loop pauses offscreen and resamples on resize. Sampling runs at 540px on the shorter side, so cost stays flat as the component grows.

entries.check: The portrait cycles from sparse outline circles and capsules at large and small cell sizes into the full-color image and back out again.

entries.name: scroll-blur-footer
entries.title: Scroll Blur Footer
entries.description: Six progressive backdrop-blur layers activate while scrolling and clear at rest. A fixed viewport-edge overlay with the original spring response, support for nested scrollers and reduced motion. Standalone React and Motion, no Framer runtime.

notes.label: Scroll activity, not scroll position
notes.description: The scrollingblur.framer.website source activates blur on any scroll event, including nested containers. After 180ms without scrolling, it clears. It does not track distance down the page.

notes.label: Progressive backdrop layers
notes.description: Six masked layers use 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 and 12px blur coefficients. The shared strength springs in with stiffness 300 and damping 30, then out with stiffness 80 and damping 26. Scrolling during the return retargets the spring.

notes.label: Decorative overlay
notes.description: Place over existing content. The component loads no images or Framer code, cannot intercept pointer input, and disables its animation when reduced motion is requested.

entries.check: Every frame shows the same soft green and black gradient with only a faint dark smear at the bottom edge in two frames, so the blur turning on during scroll and clearing at rest cannot be seen.

entries.name: vertical-dial-nav
entries.title: Vertical Dial Nav
entries.description: Scroll-linked section navigation with distance-faded labels. The active section gains weight and scale as it crosses 30% of the viewport. Click a label to scroll to its section. Pure React, with support for nested scroll containers.

notes.label: Source mechanism
notes.description: The linked Framer navigation selects the last section whose top crosses 30% of the viewport. Its labels stay in place, with distance-based opacity, active weight 500, scale 1.06 and a 0.4-second cubic-bezier transition.

notes.label: Scroll roots
notes.description: Use a scrollRoot ref for bounded sections. Selection measures that container, and link activation scrolls only that root.

notes.label: Motion and focus
notes.description: Reduced motion removes smooth scrolling and transitions. Keyboard focus remains visible. Scroll listeners and scheduled frames clean up on unmount.

notes.label: Font
notes.description: The component inherits your font styling. The demo uses the original Geist 400 and 500 files hosted on Vercel Blob.

entries.check: Scrolling walks through coloured sections while the right-side label list bolds the active section, and clicks jump to Product Designer and 3D Generalist.

entries.name: warped-gallery
entries.title: Warped Gallery
entries.description: Infinite project cards that bend as you scroll or drag. Raw WebGL renders images, video and titles together, with vertical browsing on mobile. Pure React and TypeScript, no graphics dependencies.

notes.label: One deforming card
notes.description: Media, rasterized title and generated right arrow share card UVs and inherit the same mesh deformation. The component does not load Framer, source HTML or remote JavaScript.

notes.label: Normal React composition
notes.description: Pass typed project data and place the gallery inside your own section. Headers and overlays belong outside the canvas; arbitrary React card children cannot inherit the shader bend.

notes.label: Keyboard and fallback
notes.description: Focus the region for ArrowUp, ArrowDown, PageUp, PageDown and Space. Project anchors retain normal link semantics. Unsupported WebGL gets static media links.

notes.label: Original source
notes.description: Ported from bold-lychee-277407.framer.app. The demo preserves its media and settings without Framer chrome.

entries.check: The row of project cards curves and slides through several images as the page scrolls and drags, with titles under each card.

entries.name: hover-bloom
entries.title: Hover Bloom
entries.description: Grow watercolor stems and flowers along the pointer path. An accumulating Canvas 2D painting with warm, cool, pink or custom palettes. Pure TSX, no assets or animation dependencies.

notes.label: Accumulating paint
notes.description: Translucent ellipses and strokes deposit pigment on a persistent offscreen Canvas 2D layer. No flower sprites or image assets.

notes.label: Resize and settings
notes.description: Resize keeps existing artwork centered and bottom-aligned. Changing rendering settings starts a fresh painting so callbacks cannot retain stale colors.

notes.label: Original source
notes.description: Ported from practical-assumptions-334944.framer.app. The demo uses its warm palette, cream tint and transparent dot grid.

entries.check: Watercolor stems and orange flowers grow along the pointer path and accumulate into a dense painting by the last frame.

entries.name: fluid-refraction
entries.title: Fluid Refraction
entries.description: Pointer-driven fluid refraction over an image or video. Raw WebGL simulates velocity, pressure and density, then samples the media with RGB separation and highlights. Pure React and TypeScript.

notes.label: Media, not a model
notes.description: The metallic ribbon and slogan are pixels in the demo image. The GPU simulates fluid density and samples that image with refraction, chromatic separation and highlights.

notes.label: Independent GPU resources
notes.description: Each instance owns its half-resolution velocity, pressure and density buffers. Resize and unmount release them. Offscreen/hidden scenes pause.

notes.label: Reduced motion and fallback
notes.description: Reduced motion renders the media without moving fluid. Unsupported half-float WebGL uses ordinary cover-cropped media.

notes.label: Original source
notes.description: Ported from real-result-504144.framer.app with its original image and simulation settings in the demo.

entries.check: The pointer drags refracted, chromatic streaks of the ribbon image across the frame, and the fluid trail lingers and settles.

entries.name: fisheye-scroll
entries.title: Fisheye Scroll
entries.description: A pinned poster whose oversized word is a repeating marquee sampled through a WebGL lens. Scroll slides the strip from left to right. Behind the person the lens inverts so the sides grow around the figure. In front it enlarges from the middle. Three.js, GSAP ScrollTrigger, Lenis.

notes.label: Scroll is a left-to-right marquee
notes.description: The word is painted as a repeating strip. Scroll progress offsets the sample in X, so the type slides from left to right instead of scaling in place. A 3D dolly toward the camera is a different effect.

notes.label: Behind and forward are two paints of the same strip
notes.description: Behind is an opaque pass under the cutout with an inverted lens. Forward is a second, transparent pass over the person that enlarges from the middle, so the face shows through the letterforms instead of being covered by a solid canvas. Both keeps the two stacks in lockstep on the same scroll offset.

notes.label: The lens flips with the stack
notes.description: Behind inverts the barrel so the sides grow and the centre pinches around the figure, which is the part of the word you can still see. Forward keeps a true fisheye and enlarges from the middle, because the type is now over the person and the centre is the subject.

notes.label: Owns its scroll
notes.description: By default it pins inside its own scroll container so it embeds in a bounded box. Pass embedded={false} to run it as a full-page section on the window scroll.

entries.check: The giant marquee word slides and bulges through the lens behind the pinned portrait as the page scrolls.

entries.name: fluid-reveal-carousel
entries.title: Fluid Reveal Carousel
entries.description: A rebuild of the hidden hero block on bleibtgleich.dev, where two mechanics are stacked into one. Underneath, cards orbit a ring seen edge-on: each card owns a progress value and one cycle advances every card exactly one slot, released in ring order so the turn travels as a wave rather than a rigid rotation, while distance from the front drives scale, blur, brightness, and paint order together. The ring also precesses once per spin period as every card counter-rotates, keeping artwork upright while its orbit plane turns. Over the top sits a WebGL2 cover holding one half-float field: red carries density, green and blue carry velocity. The pointer splats both, the field self-advects and diffuses through an fbm-warped sample, and the display pass maps density to alpha through a smoothstep only a hundredth wide, so the cover is solid where the field is cold and punches to nothing where the cursor has stirred it. The carousel is invisible until you wipe it into view, and the hole closes behind you. Interpolated splats keep a fast cursor from dotting the trail, a phantom pointer drifts while the real one is away, and the cover color is read back off the canvas so a CSS variable or theme swap keeps working. No dependencies.

notes.label: The carousel is the payload, the cover is the interface
notes.description: Nothing about the ring is hidden by opacity or a clip path. It renders at full strength underneath, and a WebGL canvas painted the page color sits on top. What you are moving is not a spotlight, it is a hole: the field the cursor stirs becomes alpha, so the cover is punched out where you have been and closes back as the density decays.

notes.label: One texture holds the whole simulation
notes.description: Red carries density, green and blue carry velocity, in a single half-float ping-pong pair. Three passes run it: splat writes the pointer in, the field pass self-advects and diffuses through an fbm-warped sample, and the cover pass reads only red. That is why the edge stays organic without a blur filter anywhere.

notes.label: A smoothstep a hundredth wide
notes.description: Alpha maps density through smoothstep(0.39, 0.40), a window so narrow the cover is effectively binary. Widen the gap and the hole gains a soft airbrushed halo; keep it tight and the rim reads as torn paper. It is the single most expressive number in the component.

notes.label: The ring travels as a wave
notes.description: A cycle advances every card exactly one slot, but cards are released in ring order from the front, staggered by three percent of the duration. The ring never rotates rigidly, it ripples. Distance from the front then drives scale, blur, brightness, and z-index off one value, so the back of the ring collapses into a small dark smudge instead of overlapping the front card.

notes.label: Precession, not rotation
notes.description: The ring container turns a full circle every spin period while each card counter-rotates by the same angle. Card centers sweep around a tilting orbit while the artwork itself never tips, which is what keeps a flat edge-on ring from reading as a plain horizontal slider.

notes.label: Never blank, never stale
notes.description: A phantom pointer drifts on two incommensurate frequencies once the real one has been still, so a preview is never a solid rectangle. Leaving the block wipes the field and paints one solid frame, so a paused component cannot freeze a hole in the cover.

entries.check: A white cover is punched open along the pointer trail, revealing carousel artwork underneath, and the holes close behind as the trail moves.

entries.name: sunlit
entries.title: Sunlit
entries.description: Pure CSS dappled light through window blinds and a billowing leaf canopy: progressive blur for depth, a warm floor bounce glow, a derived matrix3d light plane, and a clickable day/night switch that walks through hand-picked sunrise and sunset colors instead of a hard cut. No dependencies.

notes.label: Light is geometry, not a photo
notes.description: Horizontal shutters and vertical bars sit on a derived matrix3d plane so the dappled pattern reads as a window wall. Day and night swap shutter gap, shutter height, plane opacity, and the homography itself over a shared easing curve.

notes.label: Progressive blur sells depth
notes.description: Four stacked backdrop-filter layers, each masked with a linear gradient, keep the near wall sharp while the far canopy softens. Without the stack the leaves either look pasted on or dissolve into mush.

notes.label: Sunrise instead of a hard cut
notes.description: Toggling night runs a short color keyframe through dawn, morning, evening, and dusk, with a floor bounce glow that swaps from warm amber to cool blue. The leaf canopy keeps billowing under an SVG turbulence displacement filter.

entries.check: The dappled blind light shows on a cream wall, clicking runs through amber and brown into a navy night, and the second click returns to day.

entries.name: flow-field-text
entries.title: Flow Field Text
entries.description: A rebuild of the schemasofuncertainty.com home page. Editorial columns tile across a horizontally drag- and wheel-scrollable strip: serif headers (a NEW or type badge, a byline, an uppercase title with optional subtitle) sit above each column and translate in lockstep, while the body copy is drawn as a monospace character grid where every cell reads its glyph from a position pushed by an animated 3D simplex-noise displacement field. Legible text smears, duplicates, and dissolves into scattered fragments toward the bottom, then reforms as it breathes; a quadratic vertical mask keeps the top rows sharp. The canvas never moves, it re-samples at the scroll offset, so text flows sideways as you drag. Hover a column to pull it into an accent color, tap it to fire onSelect, and because color follows the sampled character rather than the cell, the accent bleeds across a border wherever the field borrowed a neighbor's letter. Uses the exact josephg/noisejs simplex3 and displacement constants. No dependencies.

notes.label: Sampled, not drawn
notes.description: Each grid cell reads its glyph from a noise-displaced position in the source copy, so text smears and doubles instead of a font simply animating.

notes.label: Scroll re-samples, it does not move
notes.description: The canvas is fixed; dragging or wheeling updates a scroll offset the field samples at, so text flows sideways while serif headers translate in lockstep above it.

notes.label: Quadratic vertical mask
notes.description: Displacement is zero at the top and grows with the square of depth, so headings stay legible while lower lines fray into scattered fragments, matching the source.

notes.label: Color follows the character
notes.description: The accent is decided by the sampled column's url, not the cell, so a hovered column's red bleeds across borders wherever the field borrowed a neighbor's letter.

entries.check: Letters scatter into the flow field around the pointer and reform behind it.

entries.name: blnk-agency-page
entries.title: BLNK Agency Page
entries.description: An Obys-inspired agency homepage branded BLNK: black preloader with progress and a split logo intro, fixed difference-blend header with live timezone clock and contact copy, studio caption, and three wheel-driven infinite work galleries (vertical image stack with title rail, horizontal rotated rail, and a numbered grid with center expand previews). Idle scroll snaps to the nearest project. Includes an About route. GSAP preloader; Instrument Sans; existing award-list and portfolio imagery.

notes.label: Wheel-driven infinite gallery (source scrollS)
notes.description: Matches obys.agency home: wheel/touch updates tar, RAF lerps cur (damp ~0.09 / 0.07 when snapping), list is tripled and wraps in the middle buffer, idle snaps to nearest item. Titles and meta follow the centered index.

notes.label: Logo brackets with is-spread
notes.description: Source #logo SVG halves translate ±137% when spread on Vertical/Horizontal. Removed on Grid; header wordmark shrinks on case study and About.

notes.label: Click opens work case study
notes.description: Source navigates to /work/* with a preloader-bg veil. This port runs the same fade veil then shows the #wo layout: Back, title, meta, Live Website, and a wheel-scrolled #wo-ga image column.

notes.label: Mode switch V↔H group rotation
notes.description: Source group.start rotates planes 90deg around the active item. Approximated by rotating the mode wrap while the new layout mounts.

entries.check: The black preloader draws the split logo, opens into the vertical image stack, then scrolling moves on to the horizontal image row gallery under the fixed header.

entries.name: chrome-folio-page
entries.title: Chrome Folio Page
entries.description: A dark portfolio homepage built from four scroll movements. The masthead sets a wordmark in mixed grotesque and italic serif over a liquid-chrome WebGL sphere, shaded with noise-rotated line bands under a screen-space grain pass and steered by the pointer. Scrolling grows the chrome band to full bleed while the masthead layers lift at three rates, then a cube warps in from deep Z as the mark blurs away, and a pinned fly-through sends project cards across an oversized word. Three.js, GSAP ScrollTrigger, SplitText, and Lenis.

notes.label: Noise rotates the sampling frame
notes.description: The sphere's fragment shader runs 3D value noise over the vertex position and uses that value as a rotation angle for the UV before sampling two smoothstepped sine bands. Rotating the frame is what folds the bands into the liquid-metal read, rather than sliding them.

notes.label: Linear output keeps the greys
notes.description: The renderer writes linear sRGB instead of the managed default. The shader already emits display-referred greys, so letting three convert them a second time would wash the chrome toward white.

notes.label: The camera sits inside the sphere
notes.description: A 1.5 unit sphere with the camera at z=1 puts the near surface past the camera, so the mesh fills the frame as a surface rather than reading as a ball. The band scale is tuned for that distance.

notes.label: Pointer rotation is lerped, not bound
notes.description: The pointer sets a target angle and each frame closes five percent of the remaining distance, so the chrome keeps drifting after the cursor stops instead of locking to it.

notes.label: Cube arrives from deep Z
notes.description: The cube interpolates from a 180000px Z offset with full rotations on all three axes. The first half of the pinned scroll flies it in, the second half adds a 360 degree spin on top of the settled transform.

notes.label: Cards run off one driver object
notes.description: All cards read a single tweened value rather than owning timelines. Each offsets that value by its index and clamps, then picks a segment out of a four-stop keyframe array, which is what lets them fan out and recombine without drifting apart.

entries.check: Intro, the chrome blur band, then the folio sections scroll through.

entries.name: plasma-tunnel-background
entries.title: Plasma Tunnel Background
entries.description: A full-bleed WebGL2 background that ports a compact GLSL raymarch into a copy-ready React component. A single oversized triangle drives ninety-nine accumulation steps through a sine-folded tunnel, with resolution, time, speed, intensity, and pixel-ratio controls exposed as uniforms. Pure WebGL2, no dependencies.

notes.label: One triangle feeds the whole field
notes.description: The canvas draws a single oversized triangle and lets the fragment shader decide every pixel. That keeps the component useful as a background because no mesh, texture, or scene graph has to be kept in sync with the page.

notes.label: The tunnel advances by accumulated distance
notes.description: Each frame runs ninety-nine ray steps. The inner five-fold sine warp perturbs the sample point, then the distance estimate advances z, so the brighter plasma forms from repeated near misses instead of a flat noise layer.

notes.label: Resolution is a uniform, not a CSS guess
notes.description: A ResizeObserver writes the real drawing-buffer size into u_resolution. The shader sees device pixels, while the React component still fills any CSS-sized container.

notes.label: Pixel ratio is capped for background use
notes.description: The default pixelRatio is 1.5 because ninety-nine fragment iterations are expensive at full retina size. Consumers can raise it for hero stills or lower it behind dense content.

entries.check: The red, orange and blue plasma tunnel streaks shift and pulse frame to frame behind the headline.

entries.name: type-garden
entries.title: Type Garden
entries.description: Type and stems, leaves and roses grow through each letter, from type-garden.vercel.app without its poster editor, mode switch, export and copy controls. Each key generates its growth once, from a seed the whole word shares: stems that weave in front of and behind the letter, leaves, roses that open petal by petal, and a tendril reaching toward the next letter. Space cuts that tendril so it springs back and sprouts roses, Backspace withers the last letter, Enter clears the garden. Stems lean toward the pointer, roses turn to face it, and clicking calls in a butterfly that lands on the nearest rose. Drawn on a canvas in GT Ultra, with the source's ten palettes.

notes.label: Growth decided at the keypress
notes.description: Each letter's stems, leaves and roses are generated once when its key goes down, from a seed the whole word shares, each with its own delay. Every frame draws that list at the letter's age, so growth, the sway after birth and the wither are all functions of time.

notes.label: Woven through the letter
notes.description: Each stem is cut into runs that alternate between a layer behind the letter and one in front. A rose that would sit over the letter body mostly goes behind it, so the type stays readable.

notes.label: Phone keyboards
notes.description: Predictive keyboards rewrite the field instead of sending key events. A hidden field holds a zero-width sentinel, and every change is diffed: new characters grow, removed ones wither.

notes.label: Scoped to its box
notes.description: Keys and pointer are listened for on the component, not the window, so it never takes typing from the rest of the page. It stops drawing offscreen, and reduced motion turns off the line boil.

entries.check: The canvas stays black apart from a caret and a butterfly from the click, and no typed letters or plants ever appear.

entries.name: phone-stack-carousel
entries.title: Phone Stack Carousel
entries.description: A phone in the middle of a row of cards. Drag, scroll or click a card and the row slides on a spring while the phone screen wipes to the next slide through a wobbling circle. Side cards shrink, tuck under each other and darken with distance, and videos play on the phone and on the cards. Device finish, card shape, spring feel, wipe style and background are all props.

notes.label: One spring drives everything
notes.description: Position eases toward the target index on a damped spring (silk is stiffness 110, damping ratio 1). Card offset, scale, shade, lean and the screen wipe are all read from that one position each frame, so a drag, a wheel flick and a card click land the same way.

notes.label: The screen wipe is a polygon
notes.description: The next slide is clipped to a 60-point polygon that grows from the middle of the screen's right edge. In liquid mode its radius wobbles on two sine waves around the circle, and in iris mode it stays round. The clip-path updates every frame instead of through a CSS transition, so it follows a drag.

notes.label: Sizes come from the container
notes.description: Every length is a multiple of min(1cqh, 1.95cqw), so the phone and cards keep their proportions at any box size. Give the root's parent a height.

entries.check: The card row slides and the phone screen wipes to the next slide through a circle, with side cards shrinking and tucking toward the edges.

entries.name: image-pixelation
entries.title: Image Pixelation
entries.description: An image that arrives as a few giant squares and sharpens in four steps. A canvas draws the image at 1, 1, 2 and 3 percent of its size and scales it back up with smoothing off, then the sharp image replaces it. It starts on scroll into view, on hover, on click or from a ref.

notes.label: Draw small, scale up with smoothing off
notes.description: Each step draws the image into the canvas corner at factor percent of the canvas size, then draws that corner back over the whole canvas with imageSmoothingEnabled false. The factors are the first `steps` Fibonacci numbers, then 100.

notes.label: Blocks are CSS pixels
notes.description: The canvas is not scaled by devicePixelRatio, so the squares are the same size on a 2x display. After the last step the canvas hides and the plain image shows.

notes.label: Nothing shows before the first play
notes.description: initial defaults to hidden. Set it to pixelated to show the coarsest step while waiting, or sharp to show the image.

entries.check: Every frame is solid black; no image or pixel blocks render at all.

entries.name: glyph-rain
entries.title: Glyph Rain
entries.description: Seventy-two extruded BLANK letters fall row by row into a box and pile up, drawn through an 8x8 ordered dither in one orange. matter-js runs the fall with a convex hull per letter, and three.js lights each letter and dithers it to two tones. The cursor tilts the camera and moves the light. Pass your own glyph set to drop other letters.

notes.label: Planar physics in matter-js
notes.description: Each letter's collider is the 2D convex hull of its vertices at 50 px per world unit, with friction 0.5, no bounce and gravity 4. Nine rows of eight spawn above the box at random heights and angles, so the pile is different every run.

notes.label: Two tones from a Bayer matrix
notes.description: The shader takes Lambert light from one point, compares it with an 8x8 ordered dither threshold and multiplies by the colour. Dither cells are measured against canvas height (ditherSize per height), so the pattern scales with the box.

notes.label: Stops drawing when the pile is still
notes.description: Rendering pauses off screen, and after 30 frames with no letter or camera moving. Under reduced motion the fall is solved off screen and the settled pile is drawn once.

entries.check: After about five black frames the orange dithered letters drop in and pile up at the bottom of the box, then the pile holds still.

entries.name: bunker-scene
entries.title: Bunker Scene
entries.description: A concrete bunker at night with a red BLANK sign. Behind it a hidden light flickers on, off and on again, and red god rays push through every opening in the facade. Dust drifts in front, film noise sits on top, and the camera circles slowly until the cursor takes over.

notes.label: The flicker is a hidden light source
notes.description: A red box behind the facade is the god rays light. 2.5s after load a gsap timeline turns it on, off, on, off and on in 0.05s and 0.2s steps, and each change switches the shafts through the facade openings.

notes.label: God rays at half resolution
notes.description: The light is drawn alone at half resolution, masked against scene depth, blurred radially over 100 samples and blended with screen. That is how postprocessing 6.36 drew it; later versions change the shafts, so the component carries that pass itself.

notes.label: The sign is extruded at load
notes.description: The BLANK mark is cut from SVG paths with its counters as holes and extruded over the depth the original letters had. It is scaled to their lit face area, so it is about as bright as the sign it replaces.

entries.check: The BLANK bunker goes from dim to lit as the hidden red light turns on and god rays push through the facade while the camera shifts.

entries.name: neon-sign-scene
entries.title: Neon Sign Scene
entries.description: A lightbox sign with the BLANK wordmark hangs in a dark room corner. Two seconds in it flickers on, off and on again, and the room brightens with it. Lights sliding past the room sweep across the walls while the camera orbits slowly until the cursor takes over.

notes.label: Bloom follows postprocessing 6.36
notes.description: The source shipped postprocessing 6.36, whose luminance pass weights each colour by its own luminance. 6.37 and later drop that term, so the component carries the 6.36 shader into the bloom's luminance material.

notes.label: Each material owns its environment map
notes.description: Since three r163, a material lit by scene.environment reads scene.environmentIntensity (1) instead of its own envMapIntensity. The source relies on the room at 0.08 and the sign at 0, so the cube texture goes on each material's envMap instead.

notes.label: The wordmark is drawn at load
notes.description: The sign texture is copied to a canvas and the BLANK mark is painted at the measured box of the original letters. The hosted model ships with its letters painted out, so no source typeface is left in the file.

notes.label: The first cursor move snaps
notes.description: In gsap 3.11, context.revert() reverts tweens without suppressing events, so the orbit's last update sets the camera back to the orbit start pose and overwrites the first cursor tween. The port keeps it because it is source behaviour.

entries.check: The BLANK lightbox sits dark for five frames, then switches on and stays lit with the room slightly brighter while the camera drifts.

entries.name: scribble-cursor
entries.title: Scribble Cursor
entries.description: A blue pen line that chases the pointer and redraws itself every frame with random control points, so it reads as a hand-drawn scribble. A chain of spring points follows the cursor and the line clears 100ms after the pointer stops. Tracks the whole page or only a hovered element. Canvas 2D, no dependencies.

notes.label: Redrawn every frame
notes.description: Nothing is kept between frames. The canvas clears, the spring chain steps once, and each segment is drawn as a quadratic curve whose control point lands at a new random offset, so the line wobbles in place even while the cursor holds a straight path.

notes.label: Only while moving
notes.description: Each pointer move restarts a 100ms timer. When it runs out the canvas clears, so the scribble exists only during motion and never leaves a trail behind.

entries.check: A thin wobbly blue line follows the pointer path in different spots across the frame and disappears when the pointer pauses.

entries.name: halftone-hands
entries.title: Halftone Hands
entries.description: Two hands reach in from the sides, drawn as a live halftone dot field. Each frame both poses are painted into a small offscreen field, sampled per cell and redrawn as dots quantised to six tone steps. The hands drift and breathe on a 20 second loop, cells dissolve between two poses, rows glitch sideways, and a lens under the cursor swells and darkens the dots. Eleven ink themes. Canvas 2D, no dependencies.

notes.label: Both poses are sampled every frame
notes.description: Each frame paints the left and right hand of pose A and pose B into an offscreen field two samples wide and three tall per dot, then averages the red channel per cell. A per-cell seed decides which pose a dot reads from, so the swap dissolves cell by cell instead of crossfading.

notes.label: The image must allow CORS
notes.description: Sampling reads the field back with getImageData. An image served without CORS headers taints the canvas, and the component falls back to drawing the hands directly through a fixed dot mask, without tone steps, morph or lens.

notes.label: Stills under reduced motion
notes.description: With prefers-reduced-motion the loop stops and one frame is drawn at phase zero with no intro, glitch, shimmer or lens. Drawing also pauses when the component leaves the viewport or the tab is hidden.

entries.check: Two halftone dot hands reach in from the sides, build up from sparse dots and drift and deform as the pointer passes.

entries.name: patch-cables
entries.title: Patch Cables
entries.description: A lattice of lime dots on slate that you play with the cursor. Hover and nearby dots fuse into gooey cables; drag to patch cables that fill with ink and carry signal beads from jack to jack. Every cable that closes plays a note on a pentatonic scale, through four synth voices with a shared delay and reverb. Generators can play it on their own, in time with one tempo. One WebGL2 shader and Web Audio, no dependencies.

notes.label: One shader draws the whole field
notes.description: Dots sit on the even cells of a lattice and each cell owns one diagonal. A full-screen WebGL2 fragment shader reads two small state textures and draws dots, necks and signal beads as one signed distance field, joined with a C2 smooth union so the goo has no crease.

notes.label: Joins snap, and each join is a note
notes.description: A spring per cell grows two stubs that meet in the middle. Past 0.42 of pull the cell snaps closed and holds until the pull drops under 0.2. When it closes past 0.52 it plays one note, at most one per frame and 140ms apart for Mist.

notes.label: Position picks the pitch
notes.description: The note comes from (column + rows above the bottom × 2) mod 15 on G minor pentatonic from 98 Hz (Mist uses D major pentatonic), so any gesture stays in key. Pan follows the column.

notes.label: Audio starts on the first press
notes.description: Browsers block sound before a gesture, so the AudioContext is created on the first pointer down in the canvas or a voice change.

entries.check: Lime dots fuse into gooey cables around the pointer and the drags leave patched dark cables running across the lattice.

entries.name: gyre
entries.title: Gyre
entries.description: Your words in extruded iridescent foil, running round the edge of their box, ring behind ring, until the deeper rings fade into black. Resize the box and the rings re-fit live, picking how many copies of the phrase close one lap. Move the pointer and the rings shift in parallax; scroll the wheel to push them faster. The words, separator, letter size, depth, bevel, ring spacing, lens, seven foil colours, glints, glow and grain are all props, with a light mode alongside the dark default. Three.js with opentype.js glyphs, one instanced shader, bloom and film grain.

notes.label: Every ring is the same rectangle further away
notes.description: The CPU sends each letter instance three numbers: arc position, ring and scale. The vertex shader walks a rounded rectangle to that position, bends the letter along the tangent, and pushes ring k back to depth d0 times q to the k. So the rings shrink geometrically into the fog without any per-ring layout.

notes.label: The phrase always closes the loop
notes.description: From the letter size the engine solves for how many copies of the phrase fit exactly one lap. On resize it keeps the count until another one fits clearly better, then eases between counts while holding the reading position on the nearest copy.

notes.label: Two cuts per letter
notes.description: The front three rings use a finer cut, seven curve segments, a three-step bevel and tessellated faces so the bend stays smooth. Deeper rings use a three-segment cut. Glyphs are extruded once and drawn instanced, about 300k triangles in a 820 by 560 box.

notes.label: Kerning comes from the font
notes.description: Outlines, cap height and kerning pairs are read with opentype.js, which is why it is a dependency. Three's FontLoader format has no kerning table.

notes.label: It pauses itself
notes.description: The loop stops while the box is off screen or the tab is hidden, and wakes on resize, pointer, wheel or a theme change.

entries.check: Iridescent extruded SAY IT LOUDER rings run round the box and nest into depth, rotating and shifting with the pointer and scroll.

entries.name: unfocused
entries.title: Unfocused
entries.description: An image or video under a directional lens blur that ramps from sharp at one edge to heavy blur at the other, with red and blue split apart and a fixed grain in the shadows. On mount the blur, grain and distortion run to zero over two seconds, so the picture pulls into focus. One WebGL fragment shader, no dependencies.

notes.label: The grain hashes the pixel position
notes.description: Each pixel jitters its 24 disc samples with a sine hash of its uv, so the blur reads as grain rather than a smooth gaussian. The hash is sensitive to the last bits of uv, which is why the plane, camera and index order follow the source's OGL scene.

notes.label: Rests a hair short of focus
notes.description: Like the source, the loop stops on the frame the focus pull completes without drawing it. The resting frame keeps a blur of about 0.03 at 60Hz, which reads as sharp.

notes.label: Media needs CORS
notes.description: The image or video is uploaded as a WebGL texture, so it must be same-origin or served with CORS headers. Images get mipmaps; video frames upload every frame while playing.

entries.check: The tunnel image starts heavily blurred with a red and blue split and pulls into sharp focus by the third frame, then rests.

entries.name: blur-trail-video
entries.title: Blur Trail Video
entries.description: A full-bleed video that blurs and splits into red and blue wherever the pointer has just moved, then sharpens again as the trail fades over about a second. An eased brush paints a float mask each frame, and the mask mixes the plain video with an RGB-shifted, 35-tap Gaussian blur of it. Ported from the seitaroyamazaki.com hero in WebGL2, so it runs without WebGPU.

notes.label: The trail is a float mask
notes.description: Each frame adds a soft brush at the eased pointer and multiplies the previous mask by 0.92, so a stroke fades over about 50 frames. The brush only paints while the follower trails the pointer by more than 3px, so a resting cursor leaves nothing behind.

notes.label: Blur in linear light
notes.description: The video is decoded to linear, shifted by 0.03 UV at 45 degrees per channel, blurred by a 35-tap Gaussian in two passes, mixed by the mask and encoded back to sRGB. Blur taps step in drawing-buffer pixels, so on a 2x display the blur covers half as many CSS pixels, as it does on the source.

notes.label: Frame-rate dependent, like the source
notes.description: Decay and easing are per frame. On a 120Hz display the trail fades twice as fast, which matches the original site.

entries.check: The video cycles through scenes while blurred patches with red and blue fringes appear where the pointer has just moved.

entries.description: A rotating, looping tower of modeled cassettes, one per project, rendered in WebGPU with motion blur, depth of field, bloom and film grain. notes.label: Every cassette is modeled geometry
notes.description: Shells, hubs, tape and glints are instanced meshes, and each label is a canvas texture drawn per project. The stack loops vertically while it rotates, and a post chain adds motion blur, depth of field, bloom, chromatic aberration, ACES tone mapping, grain and a vignette.

notes.label: Hover slows the stack
notes.description: Pointing at a cassette eases the rotation down and draws that project's image as fragments around it. Dragging adds spin and vertical travel; the project list beside it follows the active cassette.

notes.label: Isolated document
notes.description: The source runtime looks up elements by selector on the global document and owns window listeners. An iframe keeps those, its CSS and the WebGPU device inside this component and releases them on unmount.

entries.description: Type into a WebGL scene where letters grow moss, flowers, leaves and crystals. Six source presets, five outline fonts, adjustable size, pointer-driven motion, and image or video export. The original renderer and controls run inside an isolated document.

notes.description: The original WebGL renderer builds geometry from the selected font, then grows preset-specific instanced moss, flowers, leaves, stones or crystals across each letter. Typing changes the glyph meshes rather than masking an image onto plain text.

entries.name: soft-type
entries.title: Soft Type
entries.description: Lettering you type into. Each character is traced from Nunito Black down to its centreline and rebuilt as a chain of particles, so letters press against each other, stretch when you drag them, and pop when you press and hold. The tracing works on any glyph the device can draw, from Latin and Cyrillic to Han and Hangul, and every counter stays open because each letter's pen only fattens until a hole would close. Emoji become soft circles. Canvas 2D, no dependencies.

notes.label: Letters are traced, not stored
notes.description: Each character is drawn once in Nunito Black on a hidden canvas, thinned to a one-pixel centreline and traced into strokes. The distance transform along that centreline gives the pen radius. A rounded heavy letter is almost exactly a centreline swept by a round pen, so the rebuilt tube matches the font, and it works for any glyph the device can draw.

notes.label: Short arms survive, corner spurs do not
notes.description: Thinning grows little branches into square corners. A real stroke ends at the centre of its round cap, a pen radius inside the ink; a spur runs out to the edge. Pruning by that depth keeps the crossbar of an f and the arms of a star while removing spurs from square-ended fallback fonts.

notes.label: As bold as it can go with counters open
notes.description: Each letter's pen fattens toward the weight setting, then stops where a counter would close or lose half its area, or where an aperture like the mouth of an s would seal shut. That is why o goes heavier than e.

notes.label: Grabbing pins one particle
notes.description: The particle nearest the pointer follows it exactly and the rest of the letter gets a fifth of the same motion. Distance links, a bending constraint and a shape spring with no rotation term do the rest, so a letter stretches and drags its neighbours but always swings back upright.

notes.label: Editing keeps the letters you did not touch
notes.description: New text is matched against the letters on screen by common prefix and suffix, so typing in the middle only grows or shrinks the changed letters. After each edit every letter springs to its new slot for about four seconds, then the arrangement is yours to push around.

entries.check: Typing adds soft blob letters for blank interfaces, the letters jostle and spring into place, and the drag visibly stretches one letter.

entries.name: blur-study-grid
entries.title: Blur Study Grid
entries.description: A hundred capsules on a ten by ten grid pivot to face the pointer behind a frosted render pane, with each cell's seeded depth setting its own blur radius, diffusion ramp, opacity, and dithered edge. The original ninety-six depth samples run in one instanced WebGPU draw instead of a hundred separate meshes. Settings change live without restarting the renderer, and verified square PNGs from 2,048 to 24,000 pixels export through tiled GPU readback and stripe-streamed compression.

notes.label: Every capsule aims at the pointer
notes.description: One smoothed pointer position drives all one hundred axes. Each capsule points from its own grid cell toward that position on the render pane, so cells near the cursor foreshorten into dots while distant ones read as full strokes.

notes.label: Depth is the blur input
notes.description: Each proxy integrates ninety-six samples through its analytic capsule. The distance from the render pane drives diffusion radius, density, opacity falloff, and the dithered edge instead of applying a screen-space blur after rendering.

notes.label: One instanced draw
notes.description: The hundred transforms go into one instance buffer and a single WebGPU draw resolves every capsule, which keeps the depth integration without paying for a hundred mesh submissions.

notes.label: Depth spread is one seeded number per cell
notes.description: A Mulberry32 sequence gives each cell a single offset in the range minus a half to a half. Multiplied by depthSpread it sets how far behind the pane that capsule sits, which is why the grid reads as a field at mixed sharpness rather than a flat lattice.

notes.label: Settings are a uniform write, not a restart
notes.description: Changing settings on a mounted study writes uniforms and re-aims the capsules on the next frame. The renderer, geometry, and GPU context survive, so the prop is safe to drive from a slider.

notes.label: Render scale is the frame-rate control
notes.description: Cost is ninety-six samples per fragment times the pixel count, so a 2x display renders four times the work for the same picture. The renderScale prop caps device pixels per CSS pixel and defaults to 1. Raise it to 2 for a pixel-exact match on a high-density screen. Exports render at their own print size either way.

notes.label: Large exports never allocate the full image
notes.description: The export camera renders 1,024 by 256 pixel tiles. Rows are joined into one stripe, filtered, compressed through CompressionStream, and written to origin-private storage before the verified file downloads.

entries.check: The ten by ten grid of blurred capsules pivots so the convergence point follows the pointer to each corner and edge.

entries.name: procedural-computer-page
entries.title: Procedural Computer Page
entries.description: A full-bleed WebGL2 studio homepage whose entire background is a single raymarched fragment shader. Three tumbling 3D rings, each an analytic ellipse SDF resolved with a twelve-step Newton refinement, are smooth-unioned with a pointer-tracked crosshair and drawn twice per frame: a crisp flat line pass and a normal-shaded emboss pass, cross-faded live by pressing B. The rings orbit on a fixed fifteen second loop, the wheel injects decaying rotational velocity, the pointer is lerped toward the crosshair with exponential smoothing, and toggling dark mode inverts the grey palette. Fixed wordmark, blurred intro card, contact button, and social nav sit over the canvas. Pure WebGL2, no dependencies; keyboard shortcuts for theme (T), contact (C), and emboss (B).

notes.label: One triangle covers the whole page
notes.description: The scene is a single fragment shader rasterized over one oversized triangle at [-1,-1],[3,-1],[-1,3]. There is no geometry for the rings; every pixel independently raymarches the signed-distance field, so the cost scales with resolution, not with scene complexity.

notes.label: Rings are analytic ellipse SDFs, not sampled circles
notes.description: Each ring rotates a 3D circle by a rotation matrix and projects it, which turns it into an ellipse in screen space. The exact distance to that ellipse is solved with a twelve-step Newton iteration over the ellipse's parametric normal, then onioned to give the ring its thickness. That is what keeps the edges razor sharp at any orientation instead of blurring as they turn edge-on.

notes.label: Two passes, cross-faded by a key
notes.description: The field is evaluated twice with different line and crosshair widths: a flat pass anti-aliased with fwidth for crisp strokes, and an emboss pass that reads the SDF at four neighbours to build a surface normal and light it. Pressing B lerps uEmboss between them, so the same rings read as line art or as raised metal without a second scene.

notes.label: The loop is deterministic, the input is not
notes.description: Time is wrapped to a fifteen second period so the ring orbit is perfectly seamless. Everything reactive is added on top as an offset: the wheel feeds a velocity that decays into uScroll, the pointer is exponentially smoothed toward the crosshair, and dark mode eases uInvert. Nothing accumulates permanently, so the background never drifts out of frame.

notes.label: Dark mode is a shader uniform, not a repaint
notes.description: uInvert mixes the background from a light grey to near-black and swaps the line colour the opposite way inside the shader. Toggling the theme does not touch the DOM canvas; it eases a single float, so the whole field crossfades its palette in one smooth motion.

entries.check: The tumbling rings and crosshair reshape across frames, and pressing B switches the line art to the grey embossed pass and back.

entries.name: spiral-gallery
entries.title: Spiral Gallery
entries.description: A 3D helix of curved image tiles you scroll through. Tiles are bent into shallow arcs and stacked along a descending coil; the whole spiral idles with a slow rotation, picks up spin from scroll velocity, and tilts toward the cursor with eased parallax while the camera descends through it. A small facing shader brightens tiles as they turn to face you. Three.js + Lenis; owns its scroll container so it embeds anywhere.

notes.label: Tiles are bent geometry
notes.description: Each tile is a small grid of vertices wrapped onto a cylinder radius, not a flat plane, so the images curve with the coil. The radius eases from wide at the top to tighter at the bottom as the helix descends.

notes.label: Scroll drives spin and descent
notes.description: The spiral always rotates slowly; scroll velocity adds spin that decays, and scroll position eases the camera down the coil, so flicking the wheel spins it and holding a scroll walks you through.

notes.label: Facing brightens the image
notes.description: A small shader compares each tile's normal to the view direction, so tiles turning to face you brighten and those edge-on fade toward white, giving the rotation depth without any scene lights.

notes.label: One eased target
notes.description: Wheel, pointer drag, and touch all move the same scroll target, so the component never has competing input paths.

notes.label: Arc from geometry
notes.description: Each slide computes its wrapped distance from center, then derives scale, vertical drop, lift, and stacking from that single number.

entries.check: The arc of image frames rotates under scroll and drag, center frames lift and the title below changes to the closest slide.

notes.label: Looping plane stack
notes.description: Slides are WebGL planes assigned offsets inside a loop length. Each frame wraps through the same vertical range.

notes.label: Velocity bends vertices
notes.description: Fast input raises a distortion target, then each plane's vertices bend forward based on distance from the viewport center.

entries.name: grain-gradient-field
entries.title: Grain Gradient Field
entries.description: A section background where the grain lives inside the gradient instead of on top of it. A raymarched signed-distance shape is flat-shaded by one key light, smeared twice by noise-steered blur at quarter and half resolution, warped by a slow standing wave, dragged by a decaying pointer trail, and finally scattered by 24 random taps per pixel. Because that last pass samples the frame rather than overlaying a texture, the grain thickens where the image has contrast and disappears where it is flat, which is the tell no noise PNG can fake. Seven WebGL2 passes plus a ping-pong trail buffer, all eight shaders reproduced byte-for-byte, and every knob art-directable.

notes.label: The grain is a pass, not an overlay
notes.description: The final shader takes 24 random taps of the frame it just rendered and averages them. Because it samples the image rather than adding a texture, the scatter concentrates where there is contrast and disappears across flat ground, so the grain belongs to the gradient instead of sitting on it.

notes.label: The two blur passes run at different resolutions on purpose
notes.description: The first noise smear renders at a quarter of the canvas and the second at a half, so a 32-tap blur reaches across the whole frame for the cost of a small one. Running both at full size is slower AND tighter, which reads as a different picture.

notes.label: Nothing loops; only two clocks move
notes.description: Four of the six layers hold their clock at zero forever. The shape never rotates and the grain pattern never crawls; only the noise smear and the standing wave advance, which is why the field drifts instead of animating.

notes.label: Time is counted in frames, not seconds
notes.description: Each animating layer advances by a fixed step per rendered frame behind a 30fps gate, never by wall-clock delta. Swapping in a delta-based clock makes the drift speed depend on the display's refresh rate.

notes.label: The trail is stored as hue and value
notes.description: A ping-pong buffer writes pointer direction into hue and speed into value, decaying every frame. The pass above it converts that back into a displacement, which is how the field keeps bending for a moment after the cursor has gone.

notes.label: The scene has a fixed aspect and the box does not
notes.description: The field is drawn at a 1440x1800 ratio and anchored to the container's top-left corner, so the lit shape holds its proportions through a reflow instead of stretching with the section.

entries.check: The grainy grey and cream gradient behind the Achievements heading bends and shifts its bright lower areas as the pointer moves across it.

entries.name: grain-gradient-nav
entries.title: Grain Gradient Nav
entries.description: A floating header pill you can drag by its dot handle, that opens into a mega menu. Hovering the wordmark or a link opens a panel beneath the bar; running along the menu slides one strip sideways while its height retargets, so the whole thing reads as a single surface reshaping rather than as panels swapping. Scrolling collapses the links to zero width and shrinks the pill to the wordmark until you hover it again, and the contact panel is wider than the others, so opening it widens and re-centres the bar in the same motion. Ships the two-column link panels with arrow chips, the contact panel with a working enquiry form (text, email, option pills, textarea, drag-and-drop attachments, consent), and the Grain Gradient Field shader as the pill's surface.

notes.label: One strip, not four panels
notes.description: Every panel sits side by side in a single row that slides horizontally, while the wrapper's height animates to the panel you moved to. Both use the same 0.8s cubic-bezier(0.5, 0, 0, 1), which is what fuses a sideways slide and a vertical resize into one gesture instead of two.

notes.label: The slide only animates between panels
notes.description: Opening from closed snaps the strip into place with no transition. Animating on the way in would drag it across from wherever the last hover left it, which reads as the menu rewinding.

notes.label: The pill is max-content wide, so collapsing centres itself
notes.description: Scroll collapses the link list to zero width; because the bar is sized by its contents and centred with a transform, it re-centres for free. Deriving the bar's width from its own measured box instead feeds the min-width straight back into the next measurement and the bar grows without bound.

notes.label: The strip is absolutely positioned for a sizing reason
notes.description: Four panels of nowrap links in a flex row would set the max-content width of the bar to the sum of all of them. Taking the strip out of flow lets it contribute height but never width.

notes.label: Dragging moves position, not a transform
notes.description: The handle writes into top/left rather than a translate, because the panel below has to recompute how much vertical room is left as the bar moves. A transform would leave that measurement stale.

notes.label: Closing is a hover, not a click
notes.description: A full-screen overlay sits behind the bar while a panel is open and closes it on mouse-enter; the drag handle closes it too. There is nothing to dismiss and no click target to find.

entries.check: The pill opens into a mega menu panel that slides sideways and resizes between links, then widens into the larger contact panel with the enquiry form.

notes.description: The digit strip slides in six power4 steps while the clipped wrapper simultaneously walks one sixth of the free width per step, so the counter both rolls and travels across the bottom edge.

entries.name: inversion-lens-hover
entries.title: Inversion Lens Hover
entries.description: A WebGL image where a soft circular lens tracks the cursor and inverts a grayscale version of the image inside it, its edge broken up by 8-octave turbulence scrolling over time so the boundary churns like a living blot; the lens eases open on enter and closes when the pointer leaves or the element scrolls out of view.

notes.label: Turbulent lens edge
notes.description: The mask is a distance step whose threshold is perturbed by 8-octave time-scrolling turbulence, so the lens boundary is never a clean circle but a churning organic edge.

notes.label: Eased open and close
notes.description: Cursor position and lens radius both lerp toward their targets; leaving the element or scrolling it out of view (via IntersectionObserver) drives the radius back to zero so the lens closes smoothly.

entries.name: line-rise-text

entries.description: A long editorial page where every copy block is split into masked lines that rise from behind their baseline as it scrolls into view, while the central portrait opens from a cropped close-up; indented paragraphs preserve their opening indent after splitting.

notes.description: Blocks with a text-indent have the indent moved onto the first split line as padding, then cleared on the element, so only the opening line stays indented after the mask split.

notes.label: Grouped reveals
notes.description: A copy block can wrap several children; they split together and their lines share one scroll trigger, so a whole paragraph group rises as a single staggered sequence.

notes.label: Portrait opening

entries.name: mask-reveal-preloader

notes.description: The reveal layer composites a solid fill against the capsule SVG with mask-composite, so the shape is a hole in the fill; scaling that layer to 6x grows the hole until the hero shows through.
