entries.name: fractal-glass-hover
entries.title: Fractal Glass Hover
entries.description: A hero image seen through vertical fluted glass: a WebGL shader slices it into ~35 refracted stripes, then eased cursor movement drives a subtle parallax that pushes harder where the distortion is strongest, so the surface reads like real ribbed glass reacting to the pointer.

notes.label: Sampled refraction
notes.description: Each stripe's offset is the average of 11 samples of a mod-based displacement, giving the fluted edges a soft, glassy falloff instead of hard steps.

notes.label: Distortion-weighted parallax
notes.description: The cursor parallax is multiplied by the local distortion factor, so the image shifts more through the thickest part of the flute and the glass feels physically responsive.

entries.check: The blue portrait is sliced into fluted glass stripes, and the image shifts inside the flutes as the pointer moves.

entries.name: preloader-panel-reveal
entries.title: Preloader Panel Reveal
entries.description: A one-shot intro: two columns of masked copy and a glitching NN counter animate over a black panel while a center square grows in stepped scales to full frame, then the panel wipes up and out as the nav, hero image, and product card slide up into place.

notes.label: Stepped panel growth
notes.description: The center square is not one tween: it steps through 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, then 1 with different eases, so the fill lands in deliberate stages rather than one smooth push.

notes.label: Glitch counter
notes.description: The NN counter jumps by a random 5 to 30 each tick, clamped to the elapsed-time target, so it stutters upward to 100 instead of counting evenly.

entries.check: Masked copy and a counter animate on black as the center square grows in steps to full frame, then the panel wipes up to reveal the nav, hero image and product card.

entries.name: block-reveal-text
entries.title: Block Reveal Text
entries.description: An editorial scroll page where every copy block is split into lines and each line is uncovered by a colored bar that wipes across left to right then retracts, timed off a scroll trigger so the text reveals line by line as it enters view, with full-bleed image sections between the copy.

notes.label: Wipe then retract
notes.description: Each line's bar scales in from the left to cover the line, the line is flipped to visible under it, then the bar's origin switches to the right and it scales back out, so the reveal reads as a bar sliding through.

notes.label: Line-wrapped SplitText
notes.description: SplitText breaks each block into lines, then each line is wrapped in a positioned container that hosts its own reveal bar; the wrappers are unwound on cleanup so the DOM is left as it started.

entries.check: Black and red bars wipe across each text line and retract to leave the copy visible, with full-bleed film stills between the blocks.

entries.name: stroke-wipe-spotlight
entries.title: Stroke Wipe Spotlight
entries.description: A pinned scroll reveal where thirteen outlined pink-to-yellow strokes draw across the frame in a staggered order, swap the centered message, then erase in reverse while three bordered sparkles pop through the handoff.

notes.label: Outlined draw order
notes.description: Each source stroke is cloned into a dark outline, then both layers draw in the original alternating order with the same stagger, timing wobble, and duration cycle.

notes.label: Covered-frame handoff
notes.description: The centered copy swaps only when the longest stroke fully covers the stage; the reverse erase and three sparkle pops share that exact timeline position.

entries.check: Outlined yellow strokes sweep across the gradient until they cover the frame, sparkles pop over the covered stage, and the strokes erase to reveal the swapped THERE IT IS message.

entries.name: magnetic-spotlight-marquee
entries.title: Magnetic Spotlight Marquee
entries.description: A continuously looping row of six images that follows the pointer vertically. As the strip travels down the frame, nearby text lines rise with its wake and settle independently, preserving the source motion model and responsive composition.

notes.label: Pointer-led strip
notes.description: The marquee loops at the source speed while its vertical center eases toward the pointer inside the original 175-pixel edge limits.

notes.label: Velocity wake
notes.description: Every SplitText line reacts independently to the strip velocity and proximity, then settles toward the lifted content position using the original constants.

entries.check: The looping image strip follows the pointer up and down the frame and the nearby heading and copy lines shift in its wake.

entries.name: wordmark-spotlight-scroll
entries.title: Wordmark Spotlight Scroll
entries.description: A fixed dark stage where giant SVG wordmarks stretch vertically into one another across six scroll steps. Each project transition grows a square image from the lower-left corner, then shrinks and drifts it upward as the next wordmark takes over.

notes.label: Source SVG geometry
notes.description: The seven source SVGs are fetched from Blob, inlined, and stretched with preserveAspectRatio set to none, matching the original wordmark distortion exactly.

notes.label: Paired project motion
notes.description: Each image scales from zero during its wordmark step, then scales back to zero while drifting upward by 300 percent during the following step.

entries.check: Giant colored wordmarks stretch into one another on scroll while small square project images grow from the lower left and drift upward.

entries.name: circle-preloader-hero
entries.title: Circle Preloader Hero
entries.description: A layered circular preloader that expands through four brand colors, throws four floating cutout images across the frame, then sends them outward while the restaurant hero, navigation, footer copy, and plated centerpiece animate into place.

notes.label: Four-circle reveal
notes.description: Four full-screen circles expand with a 250ms stagger, reproducing the source color cadence before the floating item sequence begins.

notes.label: Layered handoff
notes.description: The item exits overlap the logo, navigation, elastic headline characters, footer lines, orange plate, and hero image so the preloader resolves into the final composition without a blank frame.

entries.check: Colour circles expand over black, food cutouts float around the logo, then the restaurant hero with nav, headline and the plated drink resolves.

entries.name: block-page-transition
entries.title: Block Page Transition
entries.description: A four-row page transition that wipes across the viewport, reveals a centered wordmark, swaps the full-screen scene, then retracts from the opposite edge. It includes three navigable image scenes and the original GSAP stagger and easing cadence.

notes.label: Two-sided row wipe
notes.description: Four rows scale from the left with a 75ms stagger, hold while the scene swaps, then collapse toward the right with the same cadence.

notes.label: Masked wordmark
notes.description: GSAP SplitText masks the transition wordmark by word and overlaps its rise with the incoming rows, matching the source timing.

entries.check: Clicking nav items sends stepped row blocks across the screen, shows the BLANK Studio wordmark, swaps from Genesis to Threshold to Sanctum and retracts.

entries.name: landing-counter-reveal
entries.title: Landing Counter Reveal
entries.description: A one-shot intro: a giant 0 to 100 counter scales up from the corner while a progress bar fills, then the digits slide out and a clip-path opens the hero from a center diamond to full frame before the headline characters slide in and the nav and footer words rise.

notes.label: Diamond clip-path
notes.description: The hero opens in two clip-path stages on a custom 0.9,0,0.1,1 ease: first to a centered diamond while the image scales, then to the full rectangle as it settles back to 1x.

notes.label: Masked SplitText
notes.description: Headline chars, nav words, and footer words are split with masking so they slide up and in from behind their own overflow edge; the counter itself is re-split into digits to slide out.

entries.check: The counter climbs from 50 to 100 while a small painting grows in the center, then the Canon hero opens full frame with its nav and headline.

entries.name: webgl-dissolve-scroll
entries.title: WebGL Dissolve Scroll
entries.description: A hero image progressively dissolved from the bottom up by a real-time WebGL noise field as you scroll: an fbm-driven edge eats across the frame in a colored wash while a stacked headline below fades in one word at a time.

notes.label: fbm dissolve edge
notes.description: The fragment shader compares each pixel's y against scroll progress plus a fractal-noise offset, so the wash eats across the image with a ragged, organic edge instead of a straight line.

notes.label: Word-by-word copy
notes.description: The body headline is split into word spans and each owns a slice of the copy block's scroll, fading in in sequence rather than all at once.

entries.check: Scrolling eats the MORPHOGENESIS portrait away from the bottom with a ragged noise edge into a pale wash, and the headline below fills in word by word.

entries.name: expanding-navbar-reveal
entries.title: Expanding Navbar Reveal
entries.description: A fixed 16:9 navbar card centered over a full-bleed image; scrolling the first viewport expands the card's background and link row to fill the screen while the logo FLIPs from the card's bottom center up to a pinned top bar, uncovering the hero beneath.

notes.label: FLIP logo handoff
notes.description: The logo's before and after layout is captured with GSAP Flip, then driven by scroll progress, so it travels smoothly from the card's bottom center to the pinned top bar without a layout jump.

notes.label: Scoped when embedded
notes.description: In embedded mode the root gets a transform so its position:fixed navbar is contained to the bounded stage instead of the whole viewport; drop embedded for a true full-page fixed navbar.

entries.check: The LOOSE FRAME card over the street image expands to fill the screen while the logo moves to the top bar, then shrinks back when scrolling up.

entries.name: spotlight-index-scroll
entries.title: Spotlight Index Scroll
entries.description: A pinned gallery where a centered column of images scrolls past a fixed sightline: whichever image sits on the center line brightens, a running NN/TT index counter climbs the left edge, and a stacked list of project names on the right lights up and slides one entry at a time.

notes.label: Center-line spotlight
notes.description: Each frame checks which image straddles the half-viewport line by its live bounding box and sets that one to full opacity, so the highlight tracks the scroll exactly.

notes.label: Per-name windows
notes.description: Every project name owns a 1/N slice of the scroll; inside its slice it slides up and turns white, then hands off to the next as the counter ticks over.

entries.check: The image column scrolls past the center line, the index climbs from 01/10 to 05/10, and the matching project name on the right turns white.

entries.name: liquid-stat-grid
entries.title: Liquid Stat Grid
entries.description: Three statistic cells split by dashed rules, each hiding a liquid gradient backdrop that fades up on hover while the copy inverts to white. The backdrop is a six-stage WebGL2 chain: a flat plate, a mouse-tracked colour blob, a domain warp with chromatic aberration, two noise-blur passes and a second faster warp, each stage rendering into its own framebuffer at its own resolution scale and sampling the previous one. Fully procedural, so it ships no textures and no runtime dependencies.

notes.label: Six-stage shader chain
notes.description: A flat plate, a mouse-tracked colour blob, a domain warp with chromatic aberration, two noise-blur passes and a second faster warp. Each stage renders into its own framebuffer at its own resolution scale and samples the previous stage, so the blur passes run at a quarter resolution while the warps run full size.

notes.label: Hover reveal, inverted copy
notes.description: Cells sit flat and quiet until hovered, then the gradient fades up behind the copy and the text switches to white. Set reveal to always to leave every cell running.

notes.label: Procedural, no assets
notes.description: Nothing is fetched at runtime and no textures ship with the component. The gradients exist only as shader output, so a cell costs one canvas and no network requests.

notes.label: Paused when off screen
notes.description: Each canvas holds an IntersectionObserver and skips its render loop while scrolled out of view, so three simultaneous shader chains do not burn GPU on a long page.

entries.check: Hovering each stat cell fades up its liquid gradient backdrop in pink, blue or green with white copy while the other cells stay dim.

entries.name: halftone-interface-hero
entries.title: Halftone Interface Hero
entries.description: A full-screen dark hero whose two-line wordmark is sampled into rounded halftone pixels, relit around the pointer with chromatic channel separation, and overlaid with a short RGB square-particle trail, complete with balanced navigation and a live location clock.

notes.label: Sampled, not typeset
notes.description: The two headline lines are rendered to an offscreen canvas, fitted to a 2.52:1 lockup, and sampled on a 10px desktop grid. Every visible tile comes from the text mask rather than an image asset.

notes.label: Two-layer pointer response
notes.description: Nearby dots split into three color channels while fast pointer movement sheds snapped square particles. Both effects settle independently, which keeps slow movement precise and fast movement messy.

notes.label: Idle-aware rendering
notes.description: The animation loop stops once easing and trail particles have settled, pauses outside the viewport, and leaves the typography static when reduced motion is requested.

entries.check: The halftone blank interfaces wordmark lights up with RGB channel splits and short particle trails wherever the pointer passes.

entries.name: halftone-scene-footer
entries.title: Halftone Scene Footer
entries.description: A footer whose backdrop is live video redrawn as a vertical-line halftone: a WebGL shader samples grazing sheep and a mountain ridge on a coarse grid, mapping each cell's darkness to the width of one vertical line, so the footage reads as a woven, barcode-like engraving in two inks over a warm ground plane.

notes.label: One line per cell
notes.description: A fragment shader samples the video once per grid cell, runs a levels pass (black point, white point, gamma), and converts the result to the width of a single centered vertical line. Darker cells grow wider lines, and the sweep overshoots the cell by 2% on each side so full darkness fuses into a solid field.

notes.label: Two layers, two logics
notes.description: The sheep layer draws light lines on an opaque dark field. The mountain layer inverts its levels, samples its video upside down, and sets fill opacity to zero, so the flipped bright sky becomes transparent slits revealing the warm ground plane behind the canvas, and the ridge gradient reads as a fence of stripes. The backdrop block is shorter than the band on purpose: slits above it land on the dark page and vanish, cutting the fence at one uniform height.

notes.label: Trimmed to the subject
notes.description: Cells whose sampled texel, or any texel in a two-texel ring around it, is transparent or near-black are discarded. That clips the halftone cleanly to the silhouette instead of leaving a hard rectangular video frame, and lets layers composite over each other.

entries.check: The stacked sheep and fence render as a vertical-line halftone in two inks, and the sheep shift slightly frame to frame as the video plays.

entries.name: ascii-tv-hero
entries.title: ASCII TV Hero
entries.description: A hero where a video plays as a wall of luminance-mapped ASCII glyphs inside a bulging CRT tube, with pointer movement smearing nearby cells along a chromatic trail, and scrolling expanding the set from a floating television to a flat fullscreen wall.

notes.label: Glyphs, not pixels
notes.description: Every cell samples the video once, maps its brightness to a character in a runtime-drawn atlas strip (dense ink for shadows, space for highlights), and tints the glyph with the sampled color, so the picture stays legible as type.

notes.label: A tube that scrolls away
notes.description: The screen silhouette is a signed-distance TV shape with bulged edges plus fisheye distortion, both driven by a single tvness value. Scroll progress lerps the element from its base size to the full viewport while tvness falls to zero, flattening the CRT into a plain wall.

notes.label: Pointer static
notes.description: Recent pointer positions form a decaying trail; cells near it get cell-quantized drag, chunkier re-pixelation, RGB channel separation, a scanline tear, and luma noise, which reads as a magnet held to the tube.

entries.check: The video plays as fine glyph cells inside a bulging CRT shape that smears near the pointer, and scrolling flattens it into a full-width wall.

entries.name: dust-morph-hero
entries.title: Dust Morph Hero
entries.description: A hero whose subject is a point cloud rather than a mesh: every shape is area-weighted surface sampled into the same set of points, so moving between shapes carries each point from its old surface to its new one, staggered and bowed outward so the form comes apart into dust halfway and reforms on arrival. The pointer pushes points aside in screen space and the label reveals per character on each change.

notes.label: One cloud, many shapes
notes.description: Every shape is sampled into the same number of points up front, so index i on one shape is the same point as index i on the next. A change of subject is therefore a journey per point rather than a swap of two objects, which is what lets the form survive the move.

notes.label: Every point carries a normal
notes.description: A point knows which way the surface it came from was facing, and that one attribute does three jobs: it lights the cloud, it aims the burst, and it is interpolated through the move so the shading never pops. Without it a point cloud can only ever be flat ink, because there is nothing for a light to be at an angle to.

notes.label: Area-weighted, not vertex-weighted
notes.description: Triangles are drawn in proportion to their area from a cumulative table, so density stays even instead of bunching wherever the source mesh happens to be finely tessellated. The same barycentric weights interpolate the vertex normals, so a sampled point is lit by the surface it came from rather than by its triangle facet.

notes.label: Out along the surface, in along the next
notes.description: The morph runs in three overlapping phases: burst out along the source normal, cross to a shell just off the target, settle onto it. Because both offsets follow normals, the cloud reads as the form inflating and deflating rather than as points crossing the middle of the frame.

notes.label: A wipe, not a shuffle
notes.description: Each point is delayed by its rank along an axis rather than by its seed, so the change travels through the form as a direction you can follow. The seed only jitters that slightly; let it dominate and the move dissolves into noise.

notes.label: Drag turns it, hover disturbs it
notes.description: The pointer does two different jobs and they are kept apart. Held down it orbits the subject, so you can look under and behind it, with the turn coasting after release and the tip clamped short of the poles where the drag would otherwise reverse under your hand. Merely hovering never steers anything, because an unasked-for lean toward the cursor reads as the object being handled when you only meant to look at it. The idle spin continues underneath either way, so a turned view drifts on instead of freezing where it was let go.

notes.label: The cursor is simulated, not applied
notes.description: The pointer never displaces a point directly. It drives two simulation passes whose state persists between frames: a screen space brush field that is advected along itself, diffused into its neighbours and decayed, and a spring damper per point carrying an offset and a velocity in its own texel. That persistence is the whole effect. Forces accumulate into velocity and velocity into offset, so dust keeps moving after the cursor has passed, trails behind it, and is drawn home by a spring rather than snapping back the instant the cursor leaves.

notes.label: Displaced dust chains instead of spraying
notes.description: Repulsion is aimed between straight away from the cursor and the point's own normal projected to screen, then bent along a curl noise flow read in the surface frame, and motion across that flow is damped. Points therefore gather into strands that run along the form. A plain radial push would move the same points the same distance and look like a hole being blown in a wall.

notes.label: Relative size is kept, not flattened
notes.description: Models in a set are authored at different sizes on purpose, and scaling each to a common radius throws that away: a subject that should tower over the others arrives the same size as them. One scale is applied to the whole set instead, and the camera is fitted to the median shape rather than the largest, so the typical subject fills the frame and a genuinely oversized one is allowed to overflow. Fitting to the largest would let a single wide outlier push the camera back until everything else is a detail in an empty frame.

notes.label: One flat point size
notes.description: Points are drawn at a constant size in device pixels, not scaled by depth. Perspective scaling looks obviously right and is a trap: the near face swells into heavy overdraw while the far face shrinks under one pixel, and a point under a pixel is not drawn faintly, it is not rasterized at all. The cloud loses its back half and reads as a solid crust. Depth is carried by the lighting instead.

notes.label: Resolution is a density control
notes.description: What makes a cloud read as a volume is points per pixel, so drawing at full retina resolution spreads the same points over four times the area and thins the subject to grain. Capping the pixel ratio and spending the budget on points instead is the better side of that bargain.

notes.label: The camera is solved, not tuned
notes.description: The cloud spins about one axis, so its silhouette sweeps a cylinder rather than a sphere. Measuring the distance from that axis and the height separately, then placing the camera to satisfy whichever of width or height is tighter, is what makes the subject the same size on a phone as on a desktop without ever cropping. A fitted sphere would reserve width for a depth that is never turned toward the camera.

entries.check: The point cloud forms the scales, sprays along the surface and reassembles as a DNA helix, then breaks into dust and regathers as the next shape with the headline changing each time.

entries.name: halftone-wave-hero
entries.title: Halftone Wave Hero
entries.description: A hero built around a travelling waveform of halftone dot columns: a sine envelope stretches each column until the palette reads at full saturation, then collapses it so the multiply blend drives the whole stack to black at the node. The pointer parts the wave and swells the dots, and an opening sweep unpacks it left to right.

notes.label: The black is subtractive, not painted
notes.description: Every column holds the same dots in the same palette order. Where the envelope collapses, those dots land on each other and the multiply blend takes the stack to near-black. Nothing in the code names that color, which is why the approach into it reads as a run of muddy darks instead of a swap.

notes.label: Half a cycle across the frame
notes.description: One sine at half a cycle puts a single node on screen with its antinode in the right third and the previous peak off the left edge. The whole composition, moderate left shoulder and broad right swell, falls out of where that node happens to sit, so no separate bias is needed. Drifting the phase walks the node across without any keyframes.

notes.label: A sixth of overlap, and no more
notes.description: Rows sit about 1.7 radii apart, so neighbours overlap by roughly a sixth: enough of each dot is left uncovered for its color to read at full strength, while the joins darken into seams. Columns sit slightly further apart than a dot is wide, leaving a hairline of paper so the dots stay countable. Push the row pitch under one radius and every dot is multiplied by three neighbours at once, which turns the swell to mud.

notes.label: The pointer parts the wave
notes.description: One gaussian of pointer influence drives both hover responses, so the column that opens widest is also the one whose dots swell most. Because the lift blends toward full spread, it bites hardest inside a node, where there is the most black to prise open.

entries.check: The halftone dot wave drifts its black node across the frame, and one frame shows the pointer prising the columns open on the left.

entries.name: sandy-grain-background
entries.title: Sandy Grain Background
entries.description: A near-black sandy backdrop where the pointer paints a warm amber glow that slowly burns off under a live film-grain overlay, while a small square cursor dot eases after the pointer and swells over links and buttons.

notes.label: A real fluid, not a tracked blob
notes.description: The trail lives in a ping-pong WebGL buffer that stores velocity and heat per texel. Each frame the field advects along its own velocity, diffuses, and decays before the pointer splats new energy along its path, so the glow smears and drifts like smoke.

notes.label: One canvas, three layers
notes.description: The composite pass draws the base color shaded by slow value noise, adds the amber heat additively, and overlay-blends per-pixel animated grain at 32 percent, all in a single fragment shader.

notes.label: Cursor with etiquette
notes.description: The square dot eases after the pointer at a hard 0.85 lerp, swells to a translucent 20px over links, buttons, and [data-cursor] elements, and steps aside entirely on touch devices where the native cursor returns.

entries.check: The pointer paints a warm amber glow trail across the near-black grain backdrop, and older parts of the trail fade and smear.

entries.name: aperture-zoom-hero
entries.title: Aperture Zoom Hero
entries.description: A pinned hero that pushes a window frame toward the camera on scroll: the frame and header scale up and translate in Z while a tall sky image pans behind them, then a closing headline rises into place as the zoom settles.

notes.label: Two-phase zoom
notes.description: The window scales from 1x to 4x over the first half of the pin, then holds at 4x while the header keeps translating in Z, so the frame appears to pass the camera.

notes.label: Late copy rise
notes.description: The closing headline stays fully below the fold until 66% progress, then eases up to zero, arriving only as the zoom finishes.

entries.check: The airplane window and headline scale toward the camera as the page scrolls until the frame passes out of view and the cloud sky fills the screen.

entries.name: infinite-contact-scroll
entries.title: Infinite Contact Scroll
entries.description: A looping contact sheet where each row's column gap breathes open and closed as it crosses the center line, while a pinned icon in the middle swaps to the next glyph every time a new row locks to center.

notes.label: Gap ripple
notes.description: Two overlapping ScrollTriggers per row scrub the flex gap from 1rem to 10rem and back, so a wave of spacing travels through the sheet as it scrolls.

notes.label: Center lock icon
notes.description: On every Lenis scroll event the row nearest the center line (within 25px) is found; when it changes, the pinned icon advances to the next glyph.

entries.check: Contact rows loop past the center with their column gap widening and closing, and the pinned center icon changes glyph as rows lock in.

entries.name: ribbon-stroke-scroll
entries.title: Ribbon Stroke Scroll
entries.description: A pinned intro where thick rounded ribbons draw themselves across three oversized rows on scroll, two curved ribbons sweep through and erase themselves, the palette flips to dark halfway, and the rows finally slide off screen.

notes.label: Outlined ribbons
notes.description: Every ribbon is two stacked paths: a border stroke 10px wider under the colored stroke, so each ribbon carries a dark outline as it draws in.

notes.label: Draw then erase
notes.description: The two curve ribbons animate strokeDashoffset to zero to draw, then keep going negative to erase themselves tail-first before the rows exit.

entries.check: Scrolling draws thick outlined ribbons across the rows in orange, yellow, green, blue and lilac, and a curved yellow ribbon sweeps through.

entries.name: expanding-rows-gallery
entries.title: Ingamana Projects Page
entries.description: A full project-index page where ten rows of image cards stretch from a tight 125% strip to 500% width as they scroll through view, so the entire archive feels like it zooms past the camera.

notes.label: Measured height
notes.description: The section pre-measures its height with every row at full 500% width, so the page length never jumps while rows stretch.

notes.label: Ticker-driven widths
notes.description: Row width is written every frame from each row's scroll progress on the gsap ticker, not from a ScrollTrigger, so it stays exact under Lenis smoothing.

entries.check: Rows of project images enter below the intro line and stretch wider as they scroll up through the view.

entries.name: drag-timeline-scroll
entries.title: Drag Timeline Scroll
entries.description: A five-screen horizontal layout driven by a draggable scrubber riding a tick-mark timeline along the bottom edge, easing the whole page sideways as you drag.

notes.label: Drag maps to travel
notes.description: Scrubber progress along the tick timeline maps to minus four screen-widths of container travel, eased with power3 so the page glides after the pointer.

notes.label: Generated ticks
notes.description: Fifty tick marks are appended at mount and spaced with justify-content, so the timeline stays evenly divided at any width.

entries.check: Dragging the scrubber along the bottom tick timeline slides the five-screen layout sideways through the image panels and back to the first screen.

entries.name: svg-stroke-hover
entries.title: SVG Stroke Hover
entries.description: A two-column image grid where each card draws broad SVG scribble strokes on hover and raises its title over the image.

notes.label: Stroke reveal
notes.description: Each card uses SVG paths with pathLength, so the scribble reveal runs from CSS without measuring path length in JavaScript.

notes.label: Title lift
notes.description: The card title stays tucked below the image until hover, then rises into the same frame as the broad strokes.

entries.check: Hovering cards in the grid draws broad pale scribble strokes over the image and raises titles such as Red Form Study, Material Pause and Obscured Profile.

entries.name: terminal-text-reveal
entries.title: Terminal Text Reveal
entries.description: A scroll-reactive editorial layout where paragraph words move from muted gray to bright accent and then settle into final black as each section enters view.

notes.label: Scroll parent aware
notes.description: The copy measures against the nearest scrolling parent, so it works in the bounded demo stage and fullscreen preview.

notes.label: Word progress
notes.description: Each paragraph splits into words and advances through muted, accent, and final colors as the block crosses the viewport.

entries.check: As each section scrolls in, paragraph words pass from muted gray through the green accent to black beside the engineering images.

entries.name: edge-warp-rail
entries.title: Edge Warp Rail
entries.description: A case study read sideways. Vertical scroll drives a horizontal rail of media: wheel down, swipe, or grab the rail and drag, and the whole strip travels left. Tiles bend and recede at the left and right of the frame like a page turning, so leaving the viewport reads as motion rather than a cut, and a soft edge mask dissolves them at the rim. Portrait, square, and wide frames sit in one continuous line sized by their own proportions, with short note cards set between them. Images fade up from transparent as they load. It owns its own scroll container, so it embeds in a bounded box or fills the viewport; on small screens it becomes a plain vertical stack, and with reduced motion a native horizontal scroller with no scroll hijacking. No animation library.

notes.label: Scroll becomes travel
notes.description: The component owns a vertical scroll container whose height equals the rail's overflow plus one viewport. A sticky band is pinned while the rail translates left by exactly the scroll offset, so one pixel of scroll is one pixel of sideways travel. Wheel and drag both write to that same scroll position, so every input agrees.

notes.label: The rim curls
notes.description: Each tile measures its position against the band every frame. Within the outer twelve percent on either side it rotates on Y toward a shared vanishing point and recedes on Z, with a flat middle and a fast falloff at the very edge, while a horizontal mask fades it out as it clears the frame.

notes.label: Owns its scroll, degrades cleanly
notes.description: Because it scrolls its own box rather than the window, it embeds in a bounded stage or fills the screen unchanged. Below 768px it renders a plain vertical stack, and with reduced motion it becomes a native horizontal scroller, so the warp rig only runs when it can.

entries.check: Scrolling moves the media rail left through portrait and wide frames and note cards, with tiles curling and smearing at the left and right rims.

entries.name: frame-scroll
entries.title: Frame Scroll
entries.description: A pinned hero that collapses into a drifting grid. As you scroll, the headline slides up out of frame, a second line fades in word by word, then the full-bleed image shrinks to a small rounded tile in the center. Below it, four columns of thumbnails parallax past at staggered speeds before the frame settles into a quiet outro. GSAP ScrollTrigger with Lenis; owns its scroll container so it embeds anywhere.

notes.label: One pin, phased by hand
notes.description: A single pinned ScrollTrigger drives the whole hero in onUpdate. The header lift, the word fade, the copy hide, and the image shrink each own a slice of progress, so they overlap and hand off without a timeline.

notes.label: Image becomes a tile
notes.description: The hero photo is full-bleed, then its width, height, and corner radius interpolate down to a small centered tile over the last stretch of the pin, so the frame literally shrinks rather than cutting to the next section.

notes.label: Owns its scroll
notes.description: By default it pins and parallaxes inside its own Lenis-smoothed container, so it embeds in a bounded box. Pass embedded={false} to run on the window scroll.

entries.check: The headline rises out of frame, a second line fades in, and the full-bleed photo shrinks to a small centered tile on a light ground.

entries.name: falling-tag-list
entries.title: Falling Tag List
entries.description: A hover list where each oversized name springs open, fans a small stack of thumbnails up from behind it, and drops its descriptor tags in as rounded physics pills that tumble and settle on a floor. Leaving fades the pills, collapses the row, and slides the images back down, with the name flipping between a resting and an active color. GSAP for the springs, Matter.js for the pile.

notes.label: A real physics pile
notes.description: On hover the row spins up a Matter.js world with a floor and two walls, drops a body per tag, and copies each body's position and angle onto a DOM pill every frame, so the tags actually tumble and stack instead of animating along a path.

notes.label: Springs, not eases
notes.description: The row height, the fanned thumbnails, and the collapse all use elastic easing, so opening and closing overshoot and settle. The drop is delayed a beat so the pills land into an already-open row.

notes.label: Built to be interrupted
notes.description: Entering and leaving kill in-flight tweens, fade and clear the pile, and tear down the engine, so flicking across the list never leaves stray pills or a running simulation behind.

entries.check: Hovering each name fans its thumbnails up and drops rounded tag pills that tumble and settle, then the row collapses when the pointer leaves.

entries.name: crt-display
entries.title: CRT Display
entries.description: A 3D monitor whose curved screen swaps images with a glitch. A GLB monitor model sits in a lit scene and follows the cursor with an eased parallax tilt; a CRT shader draws the tube with scanlines, an aperture-grille mask, vignette, chromatic split, and a noisy RGB tear that spikes whenever the displayed image changes, then decays. Hovering a project name loads that frame; leaving resets to default. Three.js, no animation library.

notes.label: The screen is a shader
notes.description: A curved plane re-UVs a rounded-rect geometry and runs a single fragment shader for the whole tube look: cover-fit, scanlines, aperture mask, vignette, and a chromatic split, so the image always reads as a CRT and never a flat photo.

notes.label: Swap spikes the tear
notes.description: Changing the source sets a glitch value to 1, which the frame loop decays exponentially. The shader uses it to drive horizontal hash-tear and RGB noise, so every image change arrives through static instead of cutting.

notes.label: Eased parallax tilt
notes.description: The cursor target is lerped every frame and mapped to the monitor group's rotation, so the model leans toward the pointer and glides back rather than tracking it rigidly.

entries.check: The first image shows on the monitor screen, but after switching to Waypoint, Corridor and Archive the screen stays black for half the clip before the first image returns.

entries.name: creative-clutter
entries.title: Creative Clutter
entries.description: A desk of scattered cutout objects that reflows between three named layouts. Eleven props are placed as a percentage of the board with a headline floating among them; chaos, cleanup, and notebook buttons swap the whole arrangement while GSAP Flip tweens every object and the heading from where they were to where they land, staggered from the center. Reads from its own box, so it embeds anywhere.

notes.label: Flip does the work
notes.description: Layouts are just sets of percentage coordinates. The component sets the new positions instantly, then GSAP Flip reads the before and after and animates the difference, so adding a layout is data, not animation code.

notes.label: Percent of the board
notes.description: Every object and the heading are placed as a fraction of the desk size and re-applied on resize, so the same arrangement holds its composition from a small card to a full screen.

notes.label: Staggered from center
notes.description: The transition staggers outward from the middle of the set, so a reflow reads as the desk settling rather than every piece snapping at once.

entries.check: Clicking the layout buttons reflows the scattered props and the Creative Clutter heading into new arrangements and back to the first one.

entries.name: preloader-reveal
entries.title: Preloader Reveal
entries.description: A system-boot intro that wipes away into a hero. A black preloader draws a circular progress ring and reveals stacked telemetry readouts, settling on an Engage control; engaging collapses the sheet to the left, swaps the label to a granted state, and clip-wipes through to a hero whose headline rises word by word. A white annotation backdrop underneath makes the margins read like a technical document mid-assembly. GSAP timeline with CustomEase; runs on a loop or waits for a click.

notes.label: Two sheets, one wipe
notes.description: A black preloader sits over the hero, and a white annotation backdrop sits under it. Both the preloader and the hero's white revealer collapse to the left in sequence, so the eye reads black sheet, then white document, then the hero resolving.

notes.label: The ring is the loader
notes.description: Two stacked circles draw with stroke-dashoffset: a muted track and a light progress arc that steps through staged stops, while the whole SVG rotates a quarter turn. It is a real progress gesture, not a spinner.

notes.label: Masked, hand-split text
notes.description: Readouts, labels, and the hero headline are split into masked spans in markup, not by a runtime plugin, so each line and word rises from behind its own clip with no layout flash on load.

entries.check: The ring loader and Engage control play and the sheet wipes to the white hero, but the hero media is a solid black block with no headline, and the last two frames are fully black.

entries.name: scroll-wave-gallery
entries.title: Scroll Wave Gallery
entries.description: A vertical column of photographs that sway as they scroll. Each frame rides a sum of three sine waves, a slow base swing, a faster flow, and a fine detail jitter, drifting left and right while its clip-path pinches inward at the center of the viewport. The last quarter of the set shrinks for a sense of recession. Per-image GSAP ScrollTriggers with Lenis; owns its scroll container so it embeds anywhere.

notes.label: Three waves, one drift
notes.description: Each frame's horizontal offset is the sum of a slow base swing, a faster flow, and a fine detail jitter, all keyed to the image's index and its scroll progress, so the column sways like a loose ribbon instead of a rigid grid.

notes.label: Pinch at the crossing
notes.description: The clip-path insets from both edges in proportion to distance from the viewport center, squared, so a frame is widest as it passes the middle and clipped to a sliver at the top and bottom of its travel.

notes.label: Owns its scroll
notes.description: By default it runs a Lenis-smoothed scroll inside its own container with per-image ScrollTriggers, so it embeds in a bounded box. Pass embedded={false} to drive it from the window scroll.

entries.check: The column of photographs sways left and right in a wave as the page scrolls down through it.

entries.name: scroll-tunnel-3d
entries.title: Scroll Tunnel 3D
entries.description: An endless depth tunnel of images: photos ring an ellipse four at a time and stack back along the Z axis, while wheel, drag, and idle motion pull the camera forward through them. Each layer wraps in depth so the tunnel never ends, and a per-layer black overlay fogs frames in from the far end and out as they pass the lens. One requestAnimationFrame loop, no animation library.

notes.label: Endless by wrap
notes.description: A fixed set of layers wraps in Z with a modulo, so the camera can fall forever through a handful of rings. Far frames re-enter from the back rather than running out.

notes.label: Overlay is the fog
notes.description: Depth is faked with a per-layer black overlay, not real fog. Its opacity is a hand-written curve of Z: frames fade in from the far end, hold clear through the visible band, and black out as they pass the lens.

notes.label: One target, three inputs
notes.description: Wheel, drag, and idle autoplay all push a single scroll target that is lerped into the current depth, so every input shares the same soft, mechanical follow.

entries.check: Images ringed four at a time come forward out of the dark center and grow past the lens as the scroll and drag push the camera through the tunnel.

entries.name: cappen-fluid-simulation
entries.title: Cappen Fluid Simulation
entries.description: A WebGL fluid field laid over a hard typographic hero. Pointer velocity splats into a GPU dye simulation, the display pass thresholds it into an ink mask, and idle currents keep the canvas alive even before interaction. Three.js render targets, scoped to a React component.

notes.label: The canvas is the material
notes.description: The text remains ordinary DOM. A transparent WebGL canvas sits above it with mix-blend-mode difference, so the ink reads as an optical layer rather than a background animation.

notes.label: Scoped fluid state
notes.description: Renderer, render targets, pointer listeners, resize observer, and rAF loop are all owned by the component and disposed on unmount.

notes.label: Idle splats prevent silence
notes.description: The original waits for input. This port seeds the field and adds subtle idle splats so a registry preview is never blank.

entries.check: Black ink blots follow the pointer across the white hero and reveal fragments of the inverted headline text where the fluid passes.

entries.name: ascii-image-reveal
entries.title: ASCII Image Reveal
entries.description: A gallery of photos that decode from canvas glyphs. Each tile samples its image into a luminance grid, reveals cells in a shuffled order, scrambles dense shadow characters, then fades the original photograph through the ASCII plate.

notes.label: ASCII before image
notes.description: The photo is hidden while a canvas version appears cell-by-cell. Only once the glyph grid settles does the real image fade in.

notes.label: Shadows scramble longer
notes.description: Darker sampled cells use a denser character subset and continue scrambling, giving silhouettes a noisy darkroom feel.

notes.label: Grid positions matter
notes.description: The desktop layout intentionally leaves holes across a 10-column stage. Mobile collapses to a clean two-column gallery.

entries.check: The scattered tiles fill in as glyph grids cell by cell and then fade into the grayscale photographs.

entries.name: detroit-paris-slider
entries.title: Detroit Paris Slider
entries.description: An infinite image stream whose slides grow along an exponential baseline. Wheel, drag, and idle motion push one scroll target while each poster wraps through the track and swaps images as it re-enters.

notes.label: Exponential track
notes.description: Slide edges are not linearly spaced. The width grows exponentially as a slide approaches the foreground.

notes.label: One scroll target
notes.description: Wheel, drag, and idle motion all push a single target that is lerped into the current scroll for a soft mechanical feel.

notes.label: Images wrap, not clone
notes.description: A fixed pool of slide elements changes image source when its stream index wraps back into view.

entries.check: The stepped stream of posters, small on the left and large on the right, slides along and swaps images as slides wrap back in.

entries.name: accordion-frames
entries.title: Accordion Frames
entries.description: A horizontal focus accordion: a row of thin image slats that spring open to a wide panel on hover (or tap), with a bordered focus indicator and light beams that track the open frame. Pure React, motion handled entirely by one CSS transition.

notes.label: No animation library
notes.description: Every move is one CSS transition on left/width. The component only computes geometry — the browser does the easing, so it stays cheap even with twenty panels.

notes.label: Centered as a set
notes.description: The strip is sized for exactly one open panel and centered as a whole, so it never jumps. The focused slat widens in place while the rest compress, and the indicator beams track wherever it lands.

notes.label: Touch vs. hover
notes.description: Below the breakpoint the layout thins to fewer panels and focus switches from hover to tap, so the accordion stays usable on a phone.

entries.check: A row of thin image slats opens one wide framed panel that follows the pointer from left to right and back, with the indicator lines tracking it.

entries.name: portfolio-page
entries.title: Portfolio Page
entries.description: A full single-screen portfolio with a clip-path page wipe. A dark landing reveals its wordmark line-by-line from behind masking bars, lists projects whose thumbnails slide open on hover, and carries a grainy noise overlay; clicking a project wipes the whole screen into a light project view and back. Built with Motion and AnimatePresence.

notes.label: The screen is a clip-path
notes.description: Home and project are two states of one AnimatePresence. Each enters and exits by animating a polygon clip-path, so the whole screen wipes shut and open instead of routing.

notes.label: Reveal from behind bars
notes.description: The wordmark lines sit under masking bars and slide up into view on load, staggered. It reads as type being printed rather than faded in.

notes.label: Grain ties it together
notes.description: An inline SVG noise layer animates over everything at a low opacity — no external image — giving the flat colors a filmic texture.

entries.check: The wordmark lines reveal, the project list opens a thumbnail on hover, clicking Chromatic wipes to its project page and Back wipes home again.

entries.name: material-spotlight
entries.title: Material Spotlight
entries.description: A cursor-driven material reveal on a 3D model. A near-matte standard material lit by a room-environment IBL gets a shader patch that carves a soft sphere of low-roughness, darker diffuse around the pointer's world-space hit — a wet, polished spotlight that follows the cursor and eases away. Three.js + WebGL.

notes.label: A patch, not a new shader
notes.description: onBeforeCompile splices four small chunks into MeshStandardMaterial — it keeps all of the standard PBR lighting and only overrides roughness and diffuse inside the sphere of influence.

notes.label: World-space, ray-picked
notes.description: The cursor is ray-cast onto a plane to get a world point; the fragment shader measures distance to it, so the spotlight sticks to the surface in 3D rather than sliding across the screen.

notes.label: Eased, never snapped
notes.description: Both the hit point and the activation amount lerp every frame, so the spot glides to the cursor and fades out smoothly when the pointer leaves.

entries.check: A dark polished patch moves across the Discobolus statue, from torso to legs and back, following the simulated pointer.

entries.name: hologram-walkway
entries.title: Hologram Walkway
entries.description: An isometric pixel scene in the rain. Walk a man up an endless elevated walkway with the up and down arrows; when he reaches her place, a giant pink hologram projects in, turns, greets him with her cheek on her hand and points down at him, with subtitles. Software rasteriser, a ray-marched hologram baked in Web Workers, fog, puddle reflections, an isometric city and neon signs.

notes.label: One walk, one scene
notes.description: The man starts down the walkway. When he reaches her place he stops and cannot move until she has spoken: she projects with her back to him, turns, greets him with her cheek on her hand, then points at him. Walking on plays her parting line.

notes.label: Baked, then shifted
notes.description: The walkway and the city repeat along the walk, so each bakes once and the camera takes a shifted window. Her 15 frames ray-march in Web Workers while he walks in.

notes.label: Canvas sizing
notes.description: The scene is 960 by 540 pixels and scales to its box in whole-pixel steps when the box is large enough. Give the parent a height.

entries.check: The man walks up the rainy isometric walkway, the pink hologram projects in with her back turned, turns to rest her cheek on her hand, and the Hello, handsome and What a day subtitles appear.

entries.name: watercolor
entries.title: Watercolor
entries.description: Interactive WebGPU watercolor from watercolor.bizar.ro. Paint and smudge wet pigment on procedural paper, with spreading, granulation, evaporation and a centre-out wash. Brush, water, lighting and paper controls live in the external studio panel.

notes.label: Wet and settled pigment
notes.description: Separate GPU textures carry wet pigment and deposited pigment. Water flow moves the wet paint; evaporation leaves pigment in the paper grain.

notes.label: Original shaders
notes.description: The ten WGSL modules come from watercolor.bizar.ro. The engine sizes the simulation to the component box and keeps tuning outside the canvas.

notes.label: WebGPU required
notes.description: The component shows a fallback message when WebGPU cannot initialize. Resizing or changing quality can start a new sheet.

entries.check: Three drags paint wet watercolor strokes across the paper that spread and shift hue along their length.

entries.name: ink-field
entries.title: Ink Field
entries.description: A sumi-e ink field you can paint into, rebuilt from the InkField engine's mark-making pipeline. A spring-damped brush stamps grayscale geometry, an animated wind map decides which way ink creeps, and a diffusion shader spreads it under a rule that lets ink darken a pixel but never brighten one, so strokes accumulate instead of washing out. Colour only exists at commit time, which is why the same geometry can be replayed in any of 36 pigments with optional Kubelka-Munk mixing. Seven brush modes, six diffusion behaviours, five post effects, eight flow displacement styles and a six-material metallic etching pass. All ten GLSL shaders are the originals, transcribed byte-exact.

notes.label: Ink can darken a pixel but never brighten one
notes.description: Every diffusion step takes min(here, upwind). That single rule is the whole physics: density only ever increases, so strokes accumulate and overlap instead of washing each other out, and spreading ink can never invent pigment that was not painted.

notes.label: The stroke is grayscale until you let go
notes.description: Diffusion runs on one channel so spreading ink cannot drift in hue, and colour is a separate mapping applied at commit. A live preview pass tints the draft meanwhile, which is why you see colour before the stroke has actually been encoded.

notes.label: The wind map is re-rendered every frame
notes.description: Ink does not creep in a fixed direction; it follows an animated force field regenerated against a moving clock. A mark made now diffuses along a different field than the same mark made ten seconds later.

notes.label: Diffusion runs last, so it shows up next frame
notes.description: The feedback pass is the final step of the frame, after the passes that display it. The simulation is always one step ahead of the picture, which is inherent to a ping-pong feedback system.

notes.label: Speed is subtracted from size, not multiplied
notes.description: brushSizeNow = brushSize - brushSpeed. Move fast enough on a small brush and the width goes negative, breaking the mark into the dry gaps calligraphers call flying white.

notes.label: Brush identity is stored per pixel
notes.description: On white paper a white stroke and bare paper are the same value, so a second buffer records which brush laid down each pixel. It is also why displacement runs twice: colour and identity must move together or the two drift apart.

entries.check: Drag strokes lay down black brush marks over the seeded ring, and the ink keeps spreading and softening into a diffused wash after the strokes end.

entries.name: gather-field
entries.title: Gather Field
entries.description: Points hold a picture, then throw and settle into the next one. Drift pulls one side of a line. Splash is how hard they throw. Gather is how fast they come back. Depth lifts the bright pixels off the page. Swarm remixes which point goes where. Melt keeps each point's place and lets the near layer leave first. Drop in up to four pictures. The sand is brightness, edge, and a blur, with no depth model.

notes.label: Same index, next picture
notes.description: Points are handed out along a Hilbert curve in proportion to brightness and edge. Melt keeps that order, so a point on the orb lands on the matching place in the ripple. Swarm shuffles the destination.

notes.label: Every point keeps its own flight
notes.description: Each point leaves on its own delay: in seed order for swarm, nearest layers first for melt. Splash sets how sharply the throw opens, Gather how long the whole flight takes. Turning the page mid-flight keeps every point where it is and starts the next flight from there.

notes.label: The mouse moves the sand
notes.description: Hovering leaves a short wake. The last six places the pointer passed push nearby points along the way it was moving, then let go over about a second. Dragging orbits instead, and reduced motion turns the wake, the sway and the drift off.

notes.label: Paper waits until the field is gone
notes.description: Changing paper, tone, or the point count fades the sand out, resamples, then fades in. The clear colour stays on the old paper until the fade hits zero.

notes.label: The line is a moment, not a fixture
notes.description: The split line, its wind tick, and the tip show for 1.6 seconds after the angle, offset, or side changes, then fade over the last 0.6 seconds. Drift still runs while the line is hidden.

notes.label: Brightness stands in for a depth model
notes.description: Bright pixels, edges, and a small blur decide which points exist and how far they lift. There is no neural depth pass.

entries.check: The point-cloud moon smears into a wake where the pointer passes, the points settle back, and the field throws into the next picture at the end.

entries.name: inversa-scroll
entries.title: Inversa Scroll
entries.description: A pinned hero that inverts through a masked window on scroll: the photo parallaxes up while an SVG slat-mask shrinks to punch a window through a dark overlay, the image desaturates inside it, a wireframe grid and pulsing markers fade in, copy blocks slide past, and a progress bar fills — then it re-opens to color. GSAP ScrollTrigger + Lenis.

notes.label: One scroll, many phases
notes.description: A single pinned ScrollTrigger drives everything by hand in onUpdate. Each effect — parallax, mask scale, saturation, grid, markers, copy — owns its own slice of progress with smoothstep easing, so they overlap without a timeline.

notes.label: Subtract-mask window
notes.description: The dark overlay is masked by a solid layer minus the SVG slats (mask-composite: subtract), so the slats read as a hole. Scaling the mask grows or closes that window.

notes.label: Owns its scroll
notes.description: By default it pins inside its own scroll container so it embeds in a bounded box. Pass embedded={false} to run it as a full-page section on the window scroll.

entries.check: The river photo parallaxes under scroll, then the slat mask punches a window into the dark overlay, the image desaturates and the grid with pulsing location markers fades in.

entries.name: award-list
entries.title: Award List
entries.description: A hover-reactive list of accolades: each row is a three-state shutter that slides to reveal the project credit, settling up or down by exit edge, while the hovered row's image lands on a stacking preview pile in the corner that collapses on pause and clears on leave. GSAP + Lenis.

notes.label: Three-state shutter
notes.description: Each row is a 240px column clipped to 80px: name, project, name. Hover parks it on the middle (project) band; the exit edge decides whether it settles back up or rolls down to the next name.

notes.label: Scroll keeps up
notes.description: A scroll listener re-runs the hit-test against the last cursor position, so a row entered while scrolling still opens and closes correctly instead of sticking.

notes.label: The preview pile
notes.description: Hovered rows stack their image in the corner; pause and it collapses to the most recent, leave the list and the whole pile scales away.

entries.check: Hovered rows flip to a black band showing the project name with See live, and the matching preview image stacks in the lower right corner.

entries.name: image-reveal
entries.title: Image Reveal
entries.description: A scroll-powered stack of images that dissolve into each other: a clip-path wipes each frame away to expose the next, and a band of randomized ASCII characters scatters across the seam as it travels. Pinned GSAP ScrollTrigger with Lenis; owns its scroll container so it embeds anywhere.

notes.label: Owns its scroll
notes.description: By default it pins inside its own scroll container (custom ScrollTrigger scroller + Lenis wrapper), so it embeds in a bounded box. Pass embedded={false} to drive it from the window instead.

notes.label: Decode band
notes.description: The dissolve is a density field: a solid core at the seam scattering to noise at the edges, gated per-cell by a stable hash so the static looks organic instead of uniform.

notes.label: Clip, not crossfade
notes.description: Each frame is wiped with a polygon clip-path rather than faded, so the transition has a hard moving edge — the band rides exactly that edge.

entries.check: After the intro line, scrolling wipes one grey render into the next with a hard edge while a band of orange ASCII cells rides the seam.

entries.name: mosaic-flip
entries.title: Mosaic Flip
entries.description: A wall of 3D cubes that idles with a slow random breathing, then flips over in a center-out stagger to swap project images — each picture sliced across the grid and turned tile-by-tile. A queue absorbs rapid hovers. Built with GSAP.

notes.label: Sliced, not tiled
notes.description: Every cube paints the same full image with a shifted background-position, so the grid reassembles one picture. The flip turns that picture over rather than swapping a mosaic of thumbnails.

notes.label: Hidden-face swap
notes.description: The incoming image is painted onto whichever face is currently turned away, then the grid rotates 180°. You never see the paint happen — only the reveal.

notes.label: Queued hovers
notes.description: A reveal in flight parks the next request and runs it on completion, so dragging across the list resolves to the last project instead of stuttering.

entries.check: The cube wall flips tile by tile to swap between project images as list items are clicked, including the queued rapid changes.

entries.name: fluid-mosaic
entries.title: Fluid Mosaic
entries.description: An editorial bento grid whose rows and columns are sized by a gaussian lens centered on the cursor, so the tile you approach swells while its neighbours give up their space. Photographs counter-drift inside their tiles, captions lift on hover, and the area map re-cuts itself for one to twelve items and again on narrow screens. No dependencies.

notes.label: A gaussian lens sizes the tracks, not the tiles
notes.description: Every column and row gets a weight of 1 + e^(-d^2/2r^2) x strength, where d is the distance from the cursor to that track's centre. Nothing is animated per tile: the whole layout is two lists of fr values, so a swelling tile automatically takes its space from its neighbours and the gaps stay exact.

notes.label: A 0.18fr floor stops far tracks collapsing
notes.description: At high strength the untouched tracks would shrink until their images turned into slivers. Clamping each weight to a minimum keeps the grid legible at the far edge no matter how hard the lens pulls.

notes.label: The cursor is eased, the tracks are written raw
notes.description: A rAF loop moves the pointer toward its target by a fixed fraction each frame, then writes gridTemplateColumns and gridTemplateRows imperatively. React never re-renders for motion, so the loop costs two style writes a frame regardless of tile count.

notes.label: Images are oversized by the parallax distance
notes.description: Each photograph is inset by -parallax on all sides and drifts against the cursor, so the counter-movement never exposes an edge. That drift is what makes a growing tile feel like it reveals more of the picture instead of stretching one crop.

notes.label: The area map is chosen by item count
notes.description: One table of grid-template-areas per count from one to twelve, each keeping a two-by-two hero in the top left. A ResizeObserver on the root swaps in a one or two column map below the breakpoint, so the component reflows on its own width rather than the viewport's.

entries.check: The bento tile nearest the pointer swells while its neighbours shrink, moving from the palm tree tile to the portrait row as the pointer travels.

entries.name: overlay-menu
entries.title: Overlay Menu
entries.description: A layered, curtain-style fullscreen navigation. A hamburger sweeps four colored panels down in sequence, clip-reveals a dark menu surface, and slides each link group up line-by-line. Built with a GSAP timeline and SplitText; wraps your page as a layout.

notes.label: Layered reveal
notes.description: Four curtain panels scaleY in sequence, then the dark surface clip-reveals beneath them. The overlap (a negative timeline offset) is what makes it read as depth rather than a single wipe.

notes.label: Masked line slide
notes.description: Each link is split into masked lines that slide up from behind their own clip. The slide is deliberately delayed until the curtains have mostly landed.

notes.label: Wraps your page
notes.description: The component is a layout: it renders the bar and overlay over whatever you pass as children, so it composes with an existing hero instead of replacing it.

entries.check: The hamburger sweeps green curtain panels down, the dark menu with its link columns slides in, and the second click closes it the same way.

entries.name: ascii-logo
entries.title: Interactive ASCII Logo
entries.description: A logo sampled onto a dot grid and rendered as flickering ASCII glyphs on a canvas. The cursor shoves nearby characters outward with spring physics, so the wordmark scatters and reforms as you move through it. No dependencies.

notes.label: Image fidelity
notes.description: Every glyph comes from a sampled pixel, so the source needs real contrast against the threshold. The canvas reads pixels back, so keep it same-origin or CORS-open.

notes.label: Spring, not snap
notes.description: The cursor pushes glyphs out and a spring pulls them home. Stiffness and damping decide whether the wordmark ripples or violently scatters.

notes.label: Density is brightness
notes.description: The glyph ramp maps low-to-high brightness; denser characters read as brighter pixels, so the ramp order is the contrast curve.

entries.check: The dotted ASCII module wordmark scatters around the moving pointer and reforms behind it.

entries.name: animated-footer
entries.title: Animated Footer
entries.description: A breathing, full-screen footer: two hands rendered as live, hover-reactive ASCII art with soft parallax, and a wordmark that splits and reveals on scroll. Built with GSAP and Lenis.

notes.label: Image fidelity
notes.description: The hand photos are not decorative; their contrast determines every ASCII cell. Keep CORS open so the canvas can sample pixels.

notes.label: Reveal behavior
notes.description: Fullscreen mode owns scroll with Lenis and GSAP. Embedded mode avoids scroll hijacking and reveals from an IntersectionObserver.

notes.label: Color dramaturgy
notes.description: The base glyph color should stay low and earthen while hover color carries the heat of the interaction.

entries.check: After a short intro the hands render as orange ASCII glyphs under the Blank Space wordmark, with bright hover glyphs flaring where the pointer passes.

entries.name: corridor-scene-3d
entries.title: Corridor Scene 3D
entries.description: A brutalist sci-fi corridor that rotates into view behind a stepped loading counter, then follows the pointer with slow orbital camera parallax while bloom and film grain shape the rendered scene.

notes.label: Scene-first reveal
notes.description: The loader only begins its stepped count after the GLTF and relative texture files resolve, so the overlay never reveals an empty canvas.

notes.label: Slow orbital parallax
notes.description: The camera rotates through half a turn during the intro, then eases toward a narrow pointer-driven orbit while bloom and additive grain remain in one postprocessing pass.

entries.name: drone-fleet
entries.title: Drone Fleet
entries.description: A flock of crosshair drones steering by the boids rules (separation, alignment, cohesion) plus wander. The pointer attracts the flock; clicking queues waypoints it flies to in order before returning to free roam, with dashed mesh links and live HUD telemetry.

notes.label: Boids steering
notes.description: Each drone sums separation, alignment, cohesion, and a wander term, then a turn-rate limit and speed easing keep the motion smooth so the flock reads as a coordinated fleet rather than jittering points.

notes.label: Pointer and waypoints
notes.description: The smoothed pointer is a weak attractor for free roam; clicking queues waypoints the flock chases in order, advancing once its centroid arrives, then returning to pointer-follow once the queue is cleared.

entries.check: Crosshair drones wander loosely, then gather into a tight flock that travels around the frame toward clicked points with the HUD telemetry updating.

entries.name: motion-tracking
entries.title: Motion Tracking
entries.description: A WebGPU motion-detection effect: a looping video is frame-differenced in a compute shader to build a decaying trail of movement, then rendered as tinted ASCII glyphs over the darkened footage with a bloom pass on top.

notes.label: Compute-shader frame differencing
notes.description: A WGSL compute pass diffs successive grayscale frames at quarter resolution and accumulates a decaying trail, so movement leaves a fading mask instead of a single-frame flicker.

notes.label: ASCII from motion
notes.description: The trail value picks a glyph from a rendered ASCII atlas per screen cell, tints it, and composites it over the darkened video, with a bloom pass lifting the brightest strokes.

entries.check: The grayscale waterfall video switches to a glowing blue glyph trail over the moving water while the still rocks stay dark.

entries.name: cursor-trail-scroll
entries.title: Cursor Trail Scroll
entries.description: A monochrome editorial page where the pointer paints a persistent blurred line across the full document, with scroll deltas extending the trail beneath a pinned three-column navigation.

notes.label: Document-length trail
notes.description: The canvas matches the complete editorial height, so the blurred pointer line remains painted as the page scrolls instead of being clipped to one viewport.

notes.label: Scroll-aware drawing
notes.description: Lenis scroll deltas are added to the last pointer coordinate, which keeps the trail connected even while the pointer stays still and the document moves underneath it.

entries.check: The pointer paints a blurred white figure-eight line over the GOTHIC page that stays in place, and the trail continues as the page scrolls.

entries.name: scroll-flip-cards
entries.title: Scroll Flip Cards
entries.description: A process section choreographed entirely by scroll. Three hero cards fan apart and drop away, then a pinned services panel draws the heading up from below while the same cards fly in from underneath, scale up, gather to center, and flip a half turn to reveal their service lists. Below 1000px it falls back to a static stacked layout. GSAP ScrollTrigger with Lenis, no images.

notes.label: Staggered card timelines
notes.description: Each card reads the same pinned scroll progress but offsets its start by index, so the three fly in, gather, and flip in a rolling sequence instead of moving as one block.

notes.label: Phased flight and flip
notes.description: A single card progress value is sliced into phases: rise and scale up to 60 percent, then translate to center while the inner face rotates the final 180 degrees, so motion and flip never fight for the same frames.

entries.check: The three hero cards fan and drop away, the pinned services panel brings up its heading, and the cards fly in, gather and flip to show their service lists.

entries.name: word-highlight-scroll
entries.title: Word Highlight Scroll
entries.description: Pinned copy that reads itself in as you scroll. Each paragraph section pins while its words light up one after another: a grey chip fades in, the word resolves through it, and selected keywords carry a colored pill; past 70 percent the sweep reverses. Bold color-card headlines sit between the sections. GSAP ScrollTrigger with Lenis, no images.

notes.label: Overlapping word timeline
notes.description: Each word's reveal window is offset by its index but stretched to overlap the next fifteen, so the highlight reads as a continuous sweep across the paragraph rather than fifteen discrete pops.

notes.label: Chip-then-text handoff
notes.description: A word's grey chip reaches full opacity before the letters fade in through it, and the chip only clears in the final tenth of that word's progress, so the color always precedes the reading.

entries.check: The paragraph pins while grey chips sweep across the words, the text resolves through them, and keywords keep colored pills as the next headline card scrolls away.

entries.name: split-reveal-preloader
entries.title: Split Reveal Preloader
entries.description: A one-shot intro where a studio name and numeral settle, the first letter drifts up into a compact logo mark, floating tags fade through, then the screen splits along its middle: the top lifts, the bottom drops, and a thin seam widens into the hero with a centered card whose title rolls up. GSAP timeline with SplitText and CustomEase.

notes.label: First-letter logo morph
notes.description: The opening letter of the studio name is tracked separately, sliding up and scaling to 0.75 with a heavier weight so the wordmark collapses into the compact N10-style mark instead of just fading between two logos.

notes.label: Mirrored split halves
notes.description: A duplicate overlay is pre-set to the finished logo state and clipped to the bottom half; when the seam parts, the top preloader lifts and this bottom copy drops, so the split looks like one surface tearing rather than two layers.

entries.check: NULLSPACE STUDIO types in, collapses to the N 10 mark, the screen splits along a seam and opens onto the hero with the centred NULLSPACE card.

entries.name: cursor-image-trail
entries.title: Cursor Image Trail
entries.description: A hero that spawns a trail of images behind a fast pointer. Once the cursor travels far enough inside the frame, an image is dropped at the interpolated position and slides to the live one, revealed by ten horizontal mask layers that clip open from the center out, then collapse and fade as each image ages out. Desktop only, no dependencies.

notes.label: Center-out mask reveal
notes.description: Each dropped frame is split into ten horizontal bands whose clip-paths open from a center seam outward, staggered by distance from the middle, so the image unzips rather than simply fading in.

notes.label: Distance-gated spawns
notes.description: A new frame only appears once the pointer has moved past a 150px threshold from the last drop, so the trail spaces itself by speed instead of flooding on every mouse event.

entries.check: Images drop along the figure-eight and ellipse pointer paths, open in banded strips, and age out behind the trail.

entries.name: converging-icons-text
entries.title: Converging Icons Text
entries.description: A pinned hero where a row of icons collects itself into a sentence. As you scroll, the header fades, the floating icon row lifts and scales down to caption size, then clones of each icon peel off and travel into inline slots inside a headline, moving vertically then horizontally into place, and the surrounding words fade in one by one in a shuffled order. GSAP ScrollTrigger with Lenis, desktop only.

notes.label: Clone-and-fly handoff
notes.description: The real icon row scales into caption size, then live clones take over the last leg, flying into the headline slots so the originals never have to leave their flex row and break the layout.

notes.label: Two-axis approach
notes.description: Each clone covers its vertical distance to the slot in the first half of the phase and its horizontal distance in the second, so icons drop into their line before sliding to the exact word position.

entries.check: The header fades, the icon row lifts and shrinks to caption size, small icon clones drop into slots in the headline, and the surrounding words fill in before the Link in description outro.

entries.name: dither-studio-page
entries.title: Dither Studio Page
entries.description: A full-bleed agency homepage built on dither. The whole page sits on a fixed WebGL fbm field quantised through a Bayer matrix that drifts and warps toward the cursor. A floating pill nav carries a morphing pixel mark and a per-section message, and unfolds into a full menu behind a page-wide blur. A right rail stacks a contact card and collapsible panels that follow the section in view, case rows expand in place with seeded procedural dither plates, every image slot smears into coarse pixels under the cursor, a label chases the pointer across hoverables, and a status rail pins to the bottom with a live clock. On load a counter runs to 100% before the plate dissolves from its thinnest areas outward. No media bundled, no runtime dependencies; pass footage through props.

notes.label: The page sits on a live dither field
notes.description: A fixed WebGL2 pass renders an fbm field quantised through a 4x4 Bayer matrix into drifting specks behind every section, and the field warps toward a lerped cursor. The hero blends over it with mix-blend exclusion.

notes.label: Load choreography
notes.description: A counter runs 0 to 100% on a black plate, then a second dither pass eats the plate away from its thinnest areas outward while the bracketed eyebrow settles out of random scramble glyphs.

notes.label: Mouse animations across every image
notes.description: Each media slot draws through a canvas; moving the pointer across one smears a decaying trail of coarse pixelation behind the cursor. A label pill also chases the pointer across case rows and media, summoned by data-cursor attributes.

notes.label: Chrome that follows the scroll
notes.description: The pill nav's 4x4 pixel mark morphs and its message rolls over per section, the right-rail panels open to match the section in view, and a bottom status rail keeps a live tabular-numeral clock. Case rows expand in place; videos passed via props are requantised to duotone dither every frame.

entries.name: ascii-monogram-hero

entries.description: A load-in and hero sequence where a 50 by 14 grid of solid cells dissolves in a random stagger behind a stepped glyph progress bar, revealing a giant blackletter monogram zooming from 10x scale, lit by a pointer-following light in a fogged Three.js scene and rendered entirely as monospace ASCII characters.

notes.label: The zoom starts under the cover
notes.description: The monogram begins its 6 second power3 zoom from 10x scale the moment the progress bar starts, roughly a second before the cells dissolve, so the reveal always catches it mid-flight.
